data.description:
# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and

  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit

- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite

  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive

- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer

# Intake Brief — Move level label to left (MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327)

## Problem Statement
When a business or community-space card is upgraded it shows a gold level badge
("Lvl 1", "Lvl 2", …) in the **top-right** corner of the card face. This
position competes with the cost circle / right-hand text column and reads as a
secondary stat rather than the card's primary upgrade indicator. The badge
should move to the **top-left** of the card so the upgrade level is immediately
visible in a consistent, expected position.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants to identify an upgraded card's level at a
  glance when scanning the street grid and their hand.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse the shared
  `UpgradeOverlaySpec` contract and expect a single, predictable corner
  convention for the level badge.

### User Stories
- As a player, when I look at an upgraded card on the street or in my hand, I
  see the "Lvl N" badge at the top-left of the card, so the level is obvious at
  a glance.
- As a player, the badge position is identical whether the card is shown on the
  street grid or in the hand, so I never have to re-learn where to look.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For every upgraded card (`level > 0`), the level badge is positioned at
      the card's **top-left**: in container-local coordinates (origin at the
      card centre) `levelBadge.x` is negative (left of centre) and the badge is
      **left-anchored** (`originX === 0`); the badge is no longer placed in the
      top-right (`x` must not be positive in the mirrored position). Verified by
      unit test on `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` for level 1 and level 2 cards.
- [ ] The Phaser renderer (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) renders the badge with a
      left/top origin so the text starts at the top-left inset and remains fully
      inside the card bounds (no clipping past the left or top edge); the same
      overlay path is used by street and hand cards, so both move together.
      Verified by renderer/overlay tests.
- [ ] Badge content and styling are unchanged (`Lvl N`, gold `#ffdd44`, bold,
      10px) and no badge is produced for level 0 (base) cards.
- [ ] The dynamic SVG card-face generator (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits the
      level badge at the top-left (`x` at the card's left inset,
      `text-anchor="start"`) for consistency with the overlay, with its unit
      tests updated accordingly.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (notably the module docs in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` /
      `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and the level-badge references in
      `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with all existing
      top-right level-badge expectations updated to the top-left contract.

## Constraints
- Card geometry is fixed: canonical **140 × 80** card with a **64 × 64 art zone
  at (8, 8)** (top-left) — see `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`. The
  top-left corner is therefore occupied by the card art; the badge will render
  over the top-left of the art zone (mirroring the current badge overlaying the
  top-right). This is an accepted input to the brief (see Risks & Assumptions).
- Presentation-only change — no change to upgrade rules, card state, or level
  numbers.
- Reuse the existing overlay/badge primitives and gold styling; do not introduce
  new assets or a second badge component.
- Keep the overlay spec a pure data module (no Phaser imports) so it stays
  unit-testable in Node.

## Existing State
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` builds the badge at
  `x = Math.round(width / 2 - 4)`, `y = Math.round(4 - height / 2)` (top-right,
  4 px inset) with `color: '#ffdd44'`, `fontSize: '10px'`, `fontStyle: 'bold'`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) creates the
  Phaser Text and calls `lvlText.setOrigin(1, 0)` — right/top anchored — so the
  badge sits in the top-right.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits
  `<text x="${width - 8}" y="13" … text-anchor="end">Lvl N</text>` (top-right)
  for upgraded cards. (This dynamic SVG path is exercised by unit tests; the
  runtime card face texture comes from the CSV-based template SVGs.)
- Tests asserting/pinning the badge: `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts`
  (positions the badge in the top-right), `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts`
  and `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` (badge presence/text),
  `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` (badge text).

## Desired Change
- Mirror the badge to the top-left: overlay `x = Math.round(-width / 2 + 4)`
  with `originX: 0` (and `setOrigin(0, 0)` in the renderer); `y` stays at the
  existing top inset so the badge remains on the top edge.
- Update the SVG generator badge to `x = 8` (or the chosen left inset) with
  `text-anchor="start"`.
- Update the module/JSDoc comments and the affected tests from "top-right" to
  "top-left". Exact inset values may be tuned during implementation as long as
  the badge is left-anchored in the top-left and stays inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — level-badge spec `x` / `originX` and the
  "top-right corner" comment; primary change.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays` badge
  `setOrigin(1, 0)` → `(0, 0)`; comment.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — dynamic SVG badge position /
  `text-anchor`; module doc mentions "level badge top-right".
- `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` — update the top-right
  position assertion to top-left and assert left-anchoring.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — badge position/style
  expectations.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — badge presence/absence
  alongside the cash line (position regression surface).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — SVG badge text/position.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — level-badge placement references.

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — canonical 140×80 card and the
    `(8, 8)` 64×64 art zone that occupies the top-left.
  - `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — upgrade level-up burst notes that
    reference the newly-rendered level badge.
  - `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` header — documents the overlay contract
    and the card-local coordinate system.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `MS-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — *Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card,
    growing right* (bug, medium) — closest precedent: a card-face overlay
    repositioned from centre/right to left, landed with documented placement
    assumptions.
  - `MS-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J` — *Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored
    position* (task) — companion implementation task for the sister reposition.
  - `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — *Assign a dedicated 64×64 sprite to every Main
    Street card* (medium) — touches the top-left art zone that the badge will
    now overlay.
  - `MS-0MTRRYOT6001167R` — *Change the name of Physiotherapy business card to
    Physiotherapist* (task, low) — another card-face presentation tweak with
    test/doc churn.
  - Historical (core-repo) references cited in code: `CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`
    (64×64 left-art layout) and `CG-0MP1VJVEK003I7VE` (display upgrade state on
    street-grid cards) — the layout and overlay these tests assert were
    introduced/refined there.
- **Automated report** (generated by `find-related`) — see the
  "Related work (automated report)" section retained below.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Assumption:** "top left" means the card's top-left corner, mirroring the
  current right-side inset, with the badge left-aligned. Because the 64×64 art
  zone occupies `(8, 8)`–`(72, 72)`, the badge will overlay the top-left of the
  card art. That is accepted; if the producer finds it illegible over the art, a
  subtle backing chip or a slightly different inset is a small follow-up — it
  must be raised rather than assumed.
- **Visual-regression risk:** the badge colour (`#ffdd44` gold) may have low
  contrast against some card art; mitigate during implementation by checking the
  darkest/lightest card arts and, if needed, a 1 px dark outline (recorded as a
  follow-up if it expands scope).
- **Test churn:** `upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` explicitly asserts a
  top-right position; update the assertions to the top-left contract in the same
  change rather than deleting them.
- **Scope creep:** do not restyle the badge, redesign the 64×64 layout, or
  change the cost circle / title / cash line. Record any broader card-face polish
  as separate work items.

## Open Questions
- None — the seed context (position the upgrade level badge at the top-left
  instead of the top-right) plus repo inspection of the overlay/spec/renderer
  provided sufficient signal for a clear brief. The only judgement call (badge
  overlays the top-left art zone) is recorded above as an assumption to be
  confirmed during review; no clarifying interview was required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers
- No interview conducted — the work-item description ("When a card is upgraded
  it gets a 'Lvl 1' label. Move this from the current location (top right) to
  the top left.") plus repo inspection of `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`,
  `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, and `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` provided
  sufficient signal to draft a clear brief. No assumptions were left
  unrecorded; see Risks & Assumptions for the documented top-left-art-overlay
  assumption.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MTIILDBB001F01S** – Competitive Monte Carlo harness: head-to-head simulation (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** – Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, location, lvl, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `core/docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — matched: card, current, gets, left, level, location, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, move, right, top, upgraded, when

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller challenge (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J)

**Headline:** Add a run-local **Serial Seller** challenge that completes when the player sells 3 or more street businesses in a single game, with live progress in the challenge HUD and a persistent Steam achievement consistent with the existing 12 challenges.

## Problem statement

Main Street's challenge pool currently has no goal that rewards _selling_ businesses, so the sell mechanic (Manage Card → Sell) is rarely a deliberate strategic path. This item adds a new run-local challenge, **Serial Seller**, that completes when the player sells 3 or more businesses in a single game, and shows live progress toward the goal in the challenge HUD.

## Users

- **Main Street players** choosing a strategy each run.
- **Main Street players** who need to gauge progress at a glance.
- **The designer/producer**, who wants the new challenge consistent with the existing challenge/achievement system.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a challenge that rewards selling businesses, so that a sell-and-reinvest strategy is a viable route to bonus points.
- As a player, I want to see my progress toward the challenge (e.g. "2/3 sold"), so I know how close I am to completing it.
- As the producer, I want the new challenge mapped to a persistent Steam achievement like the other 12 challenges, so the achievement set stays complete and consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New challenge template and category: `ch-serial-seller` (title **Serial Seller**, description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game.") is added to `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` with `category: 'economic'` and `rewardPoints === CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`; a new `economic` member is added to the `ChallengeCategory` union; its evaluator returns `true` iff the cumulative count of sold street businesses in the run is `>= 3`, and `false` on an empty grid.
- System integration and progress UI: the template participates in deterministic `selectChallenges` selection; completing it fires exactly once through `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` (bonus points awarded, activity-log entry written, persistent-achievement bridge invoked); the challenge HUD tracker renders live progress (e.g. `2/3`) for progress-capable challenges while challenges without progress metadata render unchanged.
- Undo/redo consistency: undoing a street sale reverts both the progress count and any challenge completion it caused; redo re-applies them exactly once (no double completion, no stale progress).
- Achievement mapping and cross-repo dependency: `ch-serial-seller` maps to achievement id `serial-seller` in `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`; the blocking dependency work item (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`, discovered-from this item) supplies the `core` submodule `electron/achievement-manifest.json` entry and the Steamworks backend API name (`TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`); the achievement completeness/drift tests pass once the dependency has landed.
- Testing and validation: unit tests cover the evaluator (empty grid, 1/2/3 sales), selection inclusion, progress metadata, HUD progress rendering, and undo/redo.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only street/tableau sales via the **Manage Card → Sell** dialog count (the `sellBusiness` path, tracked by `state.soldSlots`). Hand sales (`sellFromHand`) and the legacy `sellFromTableau` path are out of scope.
- **No new game-state field.** Reuse `state.soldSlots` (it is cumulative for the interactive path, because sold cards stay on the grid and cannot be closed) so save/load and command snapshots keep working unchanged.
- Existing tests assert **12** templates and category coverage for the 5 existing categories; these must be updated to 13 and (optionally) to assert `economic`. The category-coverage assertion for the original 5 categories must still hold.
- The achievement mapping is enforced by `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` against the launcher manifest, which lives in the **`core` git submodule (a separate repository)** — the manifest entry and Steamworks API name are handled by a separate **blocking dependency** work item `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (producer/external action), not run-local.
- The per-run selection count (`config.challengesPerRun`, default 3) and the end-of-game scoring formula are unchanged — only the template pool grows.
- The progress indicator must fit the existing challenge panel geometry (compact single-line rows); avoid layout regressions.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` defines the `ChallengeCategory` union (`synergy`, `placement`, `resource`, `upgrade`, `cross-cutting`), 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES`, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN = 3`, and `selectChallenges`/`evaluateChallenges` wrappers over the generic `@core-engine` challenge API. Evaluators are pure functions of `MainStreetState`. Selection is seeded from `config.challengesPerRun` in `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`.
- Challenge evaluation runs after every action (`evaluateChallengesAfterAction`) and at end of turn; completions are non-revocable during a run but are captured/restored by command snapshots (`captureSnapshot`/`restoreSnapshot` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, which include `soldSlots`, `challengesCompleted`, and per-challenge completion flags).
- `state.soldSlots: boolean[]` marks sold street cards; sold cards remain on the grid as inert synergy anchors and cannot be closed, so the true-count is monotonic for the interactive path and is captured in undo snapshots.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshChallengeTracker`) renders the challenge panel as compact rows: indicator + title + description, with a `Challenges (n/N)` header. There is currently no per-challenge progress display.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps every challenge template 1:1 to a persistent Steam achievement; `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` guards completeness and drift against `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- Add an `economic` challenge category and the `ch-serial-seller` template with an evaluator counting sold street businesses and an optional progress provider.
- Add an optional `progress?: (state: MainStreetState) => { current: number; target: number }` field to the `Challenge` interface and render it in the challenge HUD tracker (e.g. `2/3`), leaving progress-less challenges visually unchanged.
- Add the `serial-seller` achievement mapping and create the blocking dependency work item for the `core` manifest entry + Steamworks API name.
- Update the affected tests (template count, evaluator/selection/progress/undo, achievement mapping) and documentation.

Design note: keeping progress as an **optional Main Street-specific** field on `Challenge` (rather than extending the generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` in `@core-engine`) keeps the change surgical and avoids touching the core engine. If a second progress-capable challenge is added later, promoting the field to the generic interface can be revisited.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add `economic` to `ChallengeCategory`, add optional `progress` to `Challenge`, add the `ch-serial-seller` template (evaluator + progress).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — render progress in `refreshChallengeTracker`.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` — add `'ch-serial-seller': 'serial-seller'` to `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`.
- `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — update template count (12 → 13); add evaluator, selection, and progress-metadata tests.
- `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` — mapping completeness/drift now includes `serial-seller` (green once the child manifest entry lands).
- `tests/main-street/` challenge-HUD/scene test — add progress-rendering coverage (extend an existing scene/HUD test or add a focused one).
- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — **blocking dependency** `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (core submodule): add the `serial-seller` entry with `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and/or `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — document the new challenge/category if the challenge catalogue is described there.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — only if the progress indicator requires a layout constant tweak (avoid if possible).

## Risks and assumptions

# Add per-turn running costs to Playground, Town Fountain and Community Shelter

## Summary

Give the three remaining free-to-run Main Street community-space cards a per-turn running cost, following the Park precedent (CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK) and the producer decision of 2026-09-29. Today the Playground (`cs-playground`), Town Fountain (`cs-fountain`) and Community Shelter (`cs-shelter`) have `ongoingCost` empty → 0, so they are free synergy/reputation anchors.

## Problem statement

The Park was given a 40 coins/turn running cost to stop costless synergy spam. Three other community spaces still have no ongoing cost, so the same "free anchor" dynamic remains for their synergies:

- **Playground** (`cs-playground`) — cost 400, Entertainment, +5 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Town Fountain** (`cs-fountain`) — cost 500, Culture, +10 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Community Shelter** (`cs-shelter`) — cost 600, Service, +15 rep/turn, ongoing 0 (retiered T6→T3, CG-0MT5VZJLS000B8KI).

## Users

- **Player** — building a Playground/Fountain/Shelter cluster should feel the per-turn drain as a real strategic cost.
- **Producer / balance owner** — wants a running-cost lever on every community space, not just Park/Library/Garden/Kiosk/Public Art.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-playground`, `cs-fountain` and `cs-shelter` in the Main Street `card-data.csv` each have a non-zero integer `ongoingCost`, confirmed with the producer before merge. **Proposed mapping (agent suggestion, producer-owned — confirm or override): Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30.**
2. **Descriptions** — each updated `card-data.csv` description states the running cost using the existing wording ("Costs N coins per turn to run."), consistent with Library/Community Garden/Park, and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
3. **Deduction** — at end of turn each placed, unsold card deducts its `ongoingCost` through the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path, clamped at 0 coins and logged with an insufficient-funds log when applicable.
4. **Tooltips** — each card's community-space tooltip shows `Ongoing cost: -N/turn`; each card's cash line shows `-N`.
5. **Sold-card exemption preserved** — a sold Playground/Fountain/Shelter incurs no ongoing cost (CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA).
6. **Tests** — add distinct coverage for each card's deduction, clamping and sold-exemption (no redundant duplicates); update every test that assumes these cards are free to run, specifically:
   - `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards" uses Playground + Fountain + Shelter; re-point at cards that remain free, or rework with synthetic zero-cost card fixtures.
   - `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — "should do nothing when no community space has an ongoing cost" places a Playground; rework with a synthetic zero-cost community-space fixture.
   - `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts` — "community space card with zero ongoingCost shows \"Ongoing cost: -0/turn\"" selects `find(c => c.ongoingCost === 0)`; after this change **no shipped community space has a zero `ongoingCost`**, so it must use a synthetic zero-cost card (business/staff variants already exist).
7. **Balance sanity** — Monte Carlo and tutorial guardrails remain green; any drift is measured and reported, and no guardrail band is silently widened. The tutorial scenario places no Playground/Fountain/Shelter (verified: tutorial uses Laundromat, Local Festival, Bookshop and Library only).
8. **Docs** — update `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Ongoing/turn column), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` (special-cases) and any other doc listing these cards' running costs.
9. **Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** coins are whole integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); no fractional `ongoingCost`.
- **Data is source of truth:** the running cost lives in `card-data.csv`; tooltip, overlay and deduction derive from it.
- **Charging semantics unchanged:** placed, unsold cards only; clamped at 0; reuse the existing community-space mechanism.
- **Balance values are producer-owned:** the proposed mapping is an agent suggestion; the producer confirms or overrides before merge.
- **Zero-cost coverage must be synthetic:** after this change all eight shipped community spaces carry a non-zero `ongoingCost`, so tests of the "no ongoing cost" path can no longer rely on a shipped card.

## Existing state

- `cs-playground`: cost 400, baseIncome 0, Entertainment, rep 5, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-fountain`: cost 500, baseIncome 0, Culture, rep 10, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-shelter`: cost 600, baseIncome 0, Service, rep 15, `ongoingCost` empty.
- Other community spaces already charged: Park 40, Library 25, Community Garden 10, Health Kiosk 15, Public Art 25.
- Park precedent: commit `5ffd54a` in `tce-main-street` set `cs-park` to 40/turn and updated tests/tooltip/cash-line/docs.
- Tests that assume these cards are free: `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` ("does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards"); `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` ("should do nothing when no community space has an ongoing cost"); `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts` (`find(c => c.ongoingCost === 0)`).

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — set the three `ongoingCost` values and descriptions.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated by the suite; no SVG face change expected (community-space ongoing cost is not baked in).
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — add per-card deduction/clamp/sold coverage; rework the Playground zero-cost test.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — tooltip/cash-line coverage; rework zero-cost selection.
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — rework the zero-cost test.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`.

## Related work

- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park running cost 40/turn (precedent; producer confirmed the integer-economy mapping).
- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 — integer economy ×100 rescale.
- CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA — sold cards excluded from ongoing costs.
- CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE — community-space ongoing-cost / Park-model synergy.
- CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ — Group B community-space expansion (added these three cards).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Value assumption:** the three proposed values (20/25/30) are an agent suggestion; the producer must confirm or override before merge.
- **Balance drift:** these cards appear in Monte Carlo simulations; run the guardrails and report drift rather than widening bands.
- **Test coupling:** three existing tests rely on these exact cards (or on any zero-cost community space) being free; all must be updated/reworked (expected, not a regression). After the change no shipped community space has `ongoingCost === 0`.
- **Scope creep:** additional community-space levers (e.g. adjusting Park/Library values) are out of scope; record them as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The proposed `ongoingCost` values are Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30 (agent suggestion). Confirm these, or provide override values? — **Recommended:** accept 20 / 25 / 30 — it establishes a rising `ongoingCost` gradient (20/25/30) across the three cards while keeping them below the existing Park (40) and in the same band as Library (25) / Public Art (25). Answer: (pending producer). Source: producer decision required before merge (AC1); values are producer-owned balance data.
- **Q:** Are the three cards a single item or separate? — **Recommended:** single item — the change is one uniform data/description/edit sweep across three cards, sharing tests, docs and a single producer value decision. Answer: (agent, from seed context) single item. Source: work-item seed context.

# Storyline Coverage Analytics in Monte Carlo Harness

## Problem Statement

The Monte Carlo balance harness (MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts) currently tracks card ownership, market offers, and economy history across simulation runs, but has no visibility into storyline event coverage. Storyline events — which form branching chains with accept/reject choices — are a key game mechanic, yet the harness cannot report how often storylines fire, how deeply their chains progress, whether cycles appear, or what impact storyline choices have on win rates. This leaves the balance team blind to storyline-related balance issues.

## Users

- **Balance team / game designers**: Want to understand whether storylines are contributing positively to the game (e.g., do "Accept" choices correlate with higher win rates? Do certain storylines trigger too or too rarely?).
- **Content designers**: Want to verify that all storylines are being exercised in simulation and that chains progress reasonably (not dead-ending too quickly or cycling excessively).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline fire frequency**: The harness reports how many runs and what percentage feature each storyline (`storyline-economy`, `storyline-health`, `storyline-labor`, `storyline-restaurant`, `storyline-tax`), derived from event-choice transcript records captured during simulation runs.

2. **Chain depth tracking**: For each storyline event encountered, the harness tracks how far the chain progresses (number of consecutive chain cards pushed), reported per storyline as a distribution (mean, median, max depth) across runs.

3. **Cycle detection**: The harness detects and counts cycle occurrences (tax → tax-error → tax-inquiry → tax, per `storyline-manifest.json` edges with `cycle: true`), reporting cycle frequency per storyline and per run.

4. **Win-rate impact of choices**: For each storyline with choices (flu-outbreak, popular-menu, recession, strike-service, tax, tax-error, tax-inquiry), the harness computes the win-rate differential between "Accept" and "Reject" choices — similar to existing M2 win-rate delta pattern.

5. **Integration with existing analytics**: Storyline analytics are exposed as new functions in the balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) following the same pattern as existing metrics (G1–G8, M1–M7), with graceful degradation when storyline data is absent.

## Constraints

- **Non-blocking**: This is a deferred enhancement; it must not change existing Monte Carlo harness behaviour (strategies, termination, output format for non-storyline fields).
- **Graceful degradation**: All new storyline metrics return `null` when event-choice data is not available in run summaries (consistent with existing M4/M6/G4/G6/G7 patterns).
- **Builds on existing transcript recording**: The harness already has a lazy `recordMainStreetEvent` call path via `require('./MainStreetTranscript')`; the extension should extend this path to capture event-choice data into a new field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`.
- **No UI changes required**: Output is analytical (JSON/CSV), consistent with existing harness output.

## Existing State

- Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) runs simulations with strategies (market-greedy, demo-greedy, greedy, banking-greedy, random) and records `MonteCarloRunSummary` per seed.
- The harness already records `cardsOwned`, `marketOffers`, and `economyHistory` on run summaries (Phase 1 data).
- Storyline events with choices are resolved in-engine; `recordStorylineResolution` in `MainStreetStoryline.ts` emits `event-choice` transcript events.
- The Monte Carlo harness has a try/catch wrapper for `recordMainStreetEvent` that silently ignores failures when no recorder is wired.
- Storyline manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`) defines 5 storylines, 14 edge transitions, and 1 cycle group.
- Balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) has 8 global metrics (G1–G8) and 7 card metrics (M1–M7) with graceful degradation patterns.

## Desired Change

1. **Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary`** with a new field capturing event choices encountered during a run (event ID, choice made, chain depth at that point).
2. **Wire transcript recording** in the Monte Carlo harness so that event-choice events are captured (not just ai-action events).
3. **Add storyline analytics functions** to the balance engine:
   - `computeStorylineFireFrequency(runs)`: percentage of runs per storyline.
   - `computeChainDepthStats(runs)`: depth distribution per storyline.
   - `computeCycleStats(runs)`: cycle frequency per storyline and per run.
   - `computeChoiceWinRateDelta(runs, eventId)`: win-rate difference between Accept vs Reject.
4. **Export storyline metrics** from the balance engine barrel file.
5. **Add tests** covering all new analytics functions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary` interface; wire transcript recording for event-choice events.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — Barrel file for new storyline metrics exports.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — New analytics module for storyline-specific metrics.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — Tests for storyline analytics functions.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — Reference for storyline definitions and cycle edges (read-only).

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — write storylines (epic, completed): The parent epic that shipped the storyline system.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed): Provides the manifest data model.
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** — Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed): Provides storyline naming and feedback mechanics.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — Static validator & npm gate (completed): Validates storyline integrity.

# Intake Brief: Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (MS-0MUNB54KU005084C)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from the "write storylines" epic (`MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV`), C6
> documentation roadmap. The epic commits a generated Mermaid flowchart at
> `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`; this item renders it to a portable
> image so the graph is viewable without a Mermaid-aware renderer and links it
> from the canonical storyline doc.

## Problem statement

The storyline graph is committed only as a Mermaid source file
(`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`). Anyone reading the repository on a
plain Markdown viewer, on GitHub without Mermaid support, or in a rendered docs
artefact cannot see the graph and cannot easily tell the shape of the shipped
storylines. Rendering it to a portable SVG in a documented docs step and
linking it from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` makes the graph viewable
everywhere, without requiring a Mermaid-aware renderer.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — need to see the storyline shape at a
  glance in the docs, without installing Mermaid tooling.
  - *"As a content designer, I want the storyline graph shown as an image in the
    docs, so I can inspect the shipped chains without a Mermaid renderer."*
- **Developers / reviewers** — need the rendered graph to stay in sync with the
  committed Mermaid source so reviews trust the picture.
  - *"As a reviewer, I want a drift guard between the rendered image and the
    committed `.mmd`, so a stale graph cannot be merged."*
- **Docs build / maintainers** — need a deterministic, reproducible render step
  with no manual copy-paste.
  - *"As a maintainer, I want one documented command that regenerates the
    rendered graph, so the artefact is reproducible."*

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Finalised** per producer answers to Q1–Q3 (2026-10-07): minimal npm render
> step (A); reuse Playwright + `mermaid` devDependency (B); SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift
> guard (A).

1. **Rendered artefact** — a rendered graph image (`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`)
   is committed under `docs/main-street/` and is viewable without a
   Mermaid-aware renderer (SVG preferred; PNG only if SVG cannot be emitted).
2. **Reproducible render step** — a documented npm script renders the committed
   `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into the committed image
   deterministically (no RNG, timestamp or wall-clock input; byte-identical on
   re-run). The renderer is a **devDependency only** and does not enter the
   game bundle.
3. **Doc link** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` embeds or links the rendered
   image (in §7.2 "The shipped graph" and/or §11 "Related documents"),
   documenting the new regeneration command in the §5 tooling table.
4. **Drift guard (validation)** — an automated test/check fails when the
   committed rendered SVG drifts from the committed `.mmd`. The existing
   `.mmd`-vs-`src/card-data.csv` `--check` guard must continue to pass.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No mandatory new runtime dependency for the game** — any renderer
  dependency is a **devDependency** only and must not enter the game bundle.
  Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium (no second Chromium
  download).
- **Determinism** — the render must be reproducible from the committed `.mmd`;
  no timestamps/ids embedded in the output that would churn on every run.
- **Mermaid is the source of truth** — the `.mmd` remains the generated
  artefact of record; the image is derived, never hand-edited.
- **Licensing** — any added dependency must be permissively licensed (MIT,
  Apache-2.0, CC0). The `mermaid` package is MIT.
- **Scope** — do not redesign the graph content or the storyline model, and do
  not build a full static docs site (deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`). This
  item only renders and links the existing graph.

## Existing state (repo research)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — committed 98-line Mermaid flowchart;
  choice cards as diamonds, plain incidents as rounded rectangles, cycle edges
  as `==>`.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — generator/CLI: `--format mermaid|json`,
  `--out`, `--check` (drift guard). Deterministic (sorted ids, no RNG/clock).
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts` — CLI entry; npm script
  `storylines:graph` (`vite-node src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts`).
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` — asserts the committed `.mmd`
  matches regeneration from `src/card-data.csv` (existing drift guard).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — canonical doc. §5 Tooling, §7.2 shipped
  graph, §10 Roadmap (links this work item), §11 Related documents (links the
  `.mmd`).
- `package.json` — scripts include `storylines:graph`, `validate:storylines`;
  devDependencies already include `playwright`, `sharp`, `vite-node`/`vite`,
  `vitest`. **No `mermaid`, `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli`, `puppeteer` or docs site
  generator (mkdocs/docusaurus) is present anywhere in the repo or `core/`.**
- **There is no "docs build"** in `tce-main-street`: `docs/` is plain Markdown,
  there is no docs npm script, no mkdocs/docusaurus config, and no docs-site CI
  workflow. The only Pages workflow (`core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
  deploys the game bundle, not these docs.

## Desired change

1. **Render** the committed `.mmd` into a portable SVG via a documented,
   deterministic script/npm command that reuses the installed Playwright
   Chromium and the `mermaid` JS package (devDependency).
2. **Commit** the rendered SVG under `docs/main-street/`.
3. **Link/embed** the rendered SVG from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and
   update the §5 tooling table and §10 roadmap row.
4. **Guard** the rendered SVG against drift from the `.mmd` with a test/check;
   document the regeneration workflow.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg` — **new** rendered artefact.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — input (unchanged source of truth).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — add image embed/link; update §5 tooling,
  §7.2 shipped graph, §10 roadmap.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — possibly extend with an `svg`/render
  format or a separate renderer module.
- `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` — **new** render script (if separate

- `package.json` — new npm script (e.g. `storylines:graph:svg`) and the
  `mermaid` devDependency.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` (or a new test) — rendered-image
  drift guard.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — "write storylines" epic (completed/in review); this
  item is roadmap item C6-deferred.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — "Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema"
  (completed) — produced `storyline-graph.mmd`, the JSON manifest, and the
  existing `.mmd` drift test this item builds on.
- **MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY** — "Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift
  guard" (completed) — owns `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10 Roadmap and §11
  Related documents.
- **MS-0MUYK064P0032374** — **new**: "Static docs site that renders Mermaid docs
  at build time" (medium, discovered-from this item) — the deferred option (B)
  from Q1.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — "Fix stale example-games/main-street paths in docs
  after the src/ migration" (open) — touches the same docs tree; coordinate if
  both touch `storylines.md`.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** / **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** — sibling deferred
  storyline roadmap items (conditional options; visual authoring editor).
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** — "Editor host & read-only graph viewer" (blocked) —
  the viewer may consume the rendered graph.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** – Editor host & read-only graph viewer (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** – Storyline model & extraction seam (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: add, already, aware, build, card (+30 more)
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — matched: add, already, build, card, check (+28 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: add, already, aware, build, card (+24 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **No docs build exists (MEDIUM).** The premise "in the docs build" has no
  counterpart in the repo. *Mitigation:* Q1 answer (A) creates a minimal render
  step; the full docs-site build is deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`.
- **Determinism / review churn (MEDIUM).** SVG output can embed ids/timestamps.
  *Mitigation:* assert byte-stable output in a test; pin the `mermaid` version.
- **Headless renderer flakiness in CI (MEDIUM).** Playwright Chromium must be
  available in the test environment. *Mitigation:* reuse the already-installed
  Playwright; keep the render a dev-only npm script and guard it in tests.
- **Drift staleness (LOW).** A committed image can silently diverge from the
  `.mmd`. *Mitigation:* AC4 SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Requests to redesign the graph layout, add legends, or
  build a full docs site must be recorded as separate work items, not absorbed
  here (the docs-site request is already tracked as `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`).
- **Assumption** — SVG is the preferred format (scalable, text-searchable);
  PNG is acceptable only if the chosen renderer cannot emit SVG.
- **Assumption** — the `.mmd` stays the generated source of truth; the image is
  derived.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> **Status: answered.** Producer answers received 2026-10-07 (this session).
> Recommendations were advisory; the producer's choices are recorded below.

- **Q1 — Delivery surface ("the docs build").** *There is no docs build in
  `tce-main-street` (docs are plain Markdown; no mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages
  pipeline). How should the rendered graph be delivered?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add a minimal render step** — a new npm script that renders
    `storyline-graph.mmd` → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`, with the SVG
    committed and regenerated like the `.mmd`.
  - **(B) Create a full static docs build** (mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages) that
    renders Mermaid at build time — larger scope, new toolchain.
  - **(C) Commit a one-off rendered SVG** with no build/pipeline; document
    manual regeneration only.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — smallest change that makes the graph viewable
    everywhere and keeps it reproducible, without adopting a docs-site
    toolchain the repo does not otherwise use.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — minimal npm render step.
    **Follow-up:** option (B) tracked separately as
    `MS-0MUYK064P0032374` (medium priority). Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 — Renderer / dependency policy.** *Rendering Mermaid requires a renderer;
  none is installed, and the epic constrained new runtime deps. Which renderer?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` (`mmdc`) as a devDependency** —
    bundles a Puppeteer/Chromium download; heaviest.
  - **(B) Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium** and add the
    `mermaid` JS package as a devDependency, rendering headlessly.
  - **(C) No build-time renderer** — author/commit the SVG manually; guard
    drift only lightly.
  - **Recommended: (B)** — Playwright is already a devDependency (no second
    Chromium download) and keeps the renderer dev-only; the `mermaid` package
    is permissively licensed (MIT).
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (B)** — reuse the already-installed
    Playwright Chromium and add the `mermaid` JS package as a devDependency
    (headless render). Source: interactive reply.

- **Q3 — Drift gate scope.** *Should the new step also fail when the rendered
  SVG drifts from the `.mmd`?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Yes** — add an SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard (test/script), in addition
    to the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard.
  - **(B) No** — render the SVG but do not gate on it.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — a stale rendered graph is exactly the failure this
    item is meant to prevent.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — add an SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard
    on top of the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard. Source: interactive reply.

---

## Reopened scope: per-storyline rendering (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The combined SVG is unreadable: 71 nodes but only 11
> connected (the 5 storyline chains). Mermaid lays the 60 isolated
> (non-storyline) incidents out in a single horizontal row, producing a
> 13,268px-wide strip of tiny boxes. The producer asked to break the graph into
> pages, one parent box per page, with the standalone incidents shown as a
> compact index/table (option C). This is a **rendering/layout change only** —
> the storyline model and the committed `.mmd` source of truth are unchanged.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

7. **Per-storyline pages** — the render step emits one SVG per storyline parent
   (five: tax, health, economy, labor, restaurant), each showing only that
   storyline's chain at a readable size, committed under `docs/main-street/`.
   *Metric: five committed `storyline-graph-<slug>.svg` files; each renders the
   storyline's node/edge subset.*
8. **Standalone-incident index** — the 60 non-storyline incidents are
   represented as a compact index/table (not boxes) and are drift-guarded
   against the manifest. *Metric: index present in `storylines.md` and a test
   regenerates/comparses it from the manifest.*
9. **Docs, guards and tests updated** — `storylines.md` §7.2 embeds the
   per-storyline gallery and the index table; the render `--check` guard and
   the render tests cover every page; the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard stays
   green; the full suite passes. *Metric: full suite green; `--check` exits 0.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- One page = one **storyline** (the parent/root incident and its chain), not one
  page per choice card. This keeps the tax cycle (3 cards) together.
- "Compact index/table" is implemented as a generated Markdown table in the
  canonical doc (the natural index for plain Markdown docs), not as boxes.
- The combined `storyline-graph.mmd` remains the generated source of truth; the
  monolithic combined SVG is replaced by the per-storyline pages.

---

## Reopened scope: per-event detail tables (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The per-storyline diagrams show only the event names.
> The producer asked for much more information about each event in a storyline:
> the descriptive text, the impact on game state, and anything else critical.
> Presentation chosen: a **detail table below each diagram** (option A).

### Added Acceptance Criteria

10. **Event detail data** — the storyline manifest exposes, for every event,
    its descriptive text (`effect`), `trigger`, `tier`, `cost`,
    `target`/`targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`/`coinPercentDelta`,
    `duration`/`effectType`/`multiplier`, and the per-option `effectPolicy`;
    the JSON schema is extended and the schema drift test stays green.
    *Metric: manifest node/edge fields present; schema validation passes.*
11. **Per-event detail tables** — a generated detail table (one row per event:
    description, normalised game-state impact, choice routing) is rendered below
    each per-storyline diagram in `storylines.md` §7.2. *Metric: tables present
    and readable.*
12. **Drift guard + docs + full suite** — the detail tables are drift-guarded
    against the manifest (`npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` and a test);
    the docs are updated; the full suite passes. *Metric: `--check` exits 0;
    full suite green.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- The tables are generated between `<!-- BEGIN/END GENERATED -->` markers in
  `storylines.md`; the render step splices only the marked regions, so hand-
  written prose is never clobbered.
- Table rows lead with the event **name** (with the id) and use four columns so
  they do not collide with the §7.2 chains-table parser in the doc-drift test.
- `tier` comes from the exported `CARD_TIER_MAP`; duration fields are read from
  the `DurationEventCard` variant.

---

## Reopened scope: per-storyline docs, assets folder, richer boxes (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The detail tables added the information but the doc is
> still not readable: `storylines.md` is now long, and the diagram boxes show
> only the name/id. Producer requirements: separate each storyline's `.md` from
> `storylines.md`; move the SVGs into an assets folder; and put a brief
> description + game-state impact inside each box.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

13. **Per-storyline documents** — each storyline has its own committed Markdown
    document (`docs/main-street/storylines/<slug>.md`) containing its diagram
    and per-event detail table; `storylines.md` links to them and no longer
    embeds the diagrams/tables. *Metric: 5 per-storyline docs; `storylines.md`
    contains links, not embeds.*
14. **Assets folder** — the rendered SVGs live under
    `docs/main-street/assets/` (`storyline-graph-<slug>.svg`) and every
    reference (docs, tests, guards) uses the new path. *Metric: no committed
    SVG remains at the old path; links resolve.*
15. **Readable boxes** — each diagram box shows a brief form of the event's
    description and its game-state impact (not just name/id). *Metric: rendered
    SVG node labels contain the brief text and impact; drift guard updated.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- "Brief form of the description" = the first sentence of the card's `effect`
  text, truncated to a bounded length.
- "Game-state impact" = the normalised impact already computed for the detail
  tables (coin/reputation deltas, proportional coin loss, duration multiplier).
- Assets live at `docs/main-street/assets/` (no existing docs-asset convention;
  `screenshots/` is unrelated and specific to screenshots).
- The per-storyline docs are generated (like the incident index) and
  drift-guarded, so the tables/diagrams never drift from the manifest.

---

## Reopened scope: actionable drift-test failures (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** When a drift guard fails it names the stale artefact but
> does not say how to fix it. The failure output must include the command(s) to
> regenerate the committed docs.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

16. **Actionable test failures** — every storyline-docs drift assertion emits
    the exact regeneration command(s) in its failure output (Vitest custom
    message), so a developer can fix a stale artefact without reading the
    source. *Metric: failing assertion output contains
    `npm run storylines:graph:svg` (and the `.mmd`/JSON commands where
    relevant).*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- Use Vitest's `expect(actual, message)` custom message so the hint precedes the
  value diff.
- One shared hint constant per test file, tailored to the artefacts it guards:
  - SVG/doc drift → `npm run storylines:graph:svg`
  - `.mmd`/manifest drift → `npm run storylines:graph -- --format mermaid|json`
