# Piggyback on other players' organiser actions

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, when one player organises a town-wide event such as a Local Festival, the benefits are currently routed only to that acting player's own wallet (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects`). There is no way for the other player(s) to participate in, or benefit from, an event that thematically belongs to the whole town. This makes events feel private rather than communal and removes a legible, interesting per-event decision from the non-acting player.

## Users

Primary user: the **human player in competitive mode**, who wants a meaningful reactive decision when the AI organises a town event.

- As the human player, when the AI organises a festival, I want to choose whether to co-fund it so that I can earn the full reward, or simply enjoy the spill-over benefit for free.
- As the human player, I want the trade-off to be explicit (coins and action cost vs. reward share) so the decision is legible.
- Secondary user: the **AI seat**, which needs a deterministic policy for the same decision so headless Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible.

## Proposed mechanic (design summary)

When a player plays a **piggyback-eligible Investment event** (an "organiser" event — e.g. Local Festival, Harvest Festival) during their MarketPhase, every **other active player** receives a 50% share of that event's rewards **automatically**, and is offered the single choice to **join fully**:

| Option | Cost | Reward |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Join fully** | **150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event** (paid from the piggybacker's own coins); **no action point is spent** | **100%** of the event's rewards |
| **Free-ride (automatic default)** | Nothing | **50%** of the event's rewards, granted automatically |

- The free-ride 50% is always applied, so there is **no "decline everything" option** and no prompt to refuse it — the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade 50% → 100%.
- Joining fully does **not** consume an action point; the seed's "take an additional action" means the player participates in the event (an additional participant), not that a budget action is spent.
- Rewards (coin + reputation) are computed on the **piggybacker's own board**, consistent with the existing per-owner event routing (`SpecificSynergy` rewards count the owner's own matching businesses), then scaled to 100% (join fully) or 50% (free-ride).
- The cost baseline is the amount the acting player **actually paid** for the event (after any cost discounts the acting player holds), not necessarily the card's nominal listed cost.
- If the piggybacker cannot afford 150% of that cost, the join-fully option is unavailable and the 50% free-ride applies.
- The acting player's own reward, and the shared market/incident deck, are unaffected by piggyback decisions.
- The mechanic applies **only in competitive mode (N≥2)**; single-player (N=1) has no other players and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Eligibility & trigger.** When an active player plays a piggyback-eligible **organiser** Investment event during their MarketPhase in competitive mode (N≥2), every other non-eliminated player automatically receives the 50% free-ride share and is offered the join-fully upgrade for that event; playing a non-eligible event (or any event in N=1) produces no share and no prompt. Verified by unit tests over a flagged eligible card and an unflagged card.
- [ ] **AC2 — Join-fully tier.** Choosing "join fully" deducts exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event from the piggybacker's own coin balance (and **no action point**), then credits the piggybacker 100% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board). The option is unavailable (and never partially charged) when the piggybacker cannot afford the cost. Verified by unit tests asserting exact before/after coin and reputation values and an unchanged action budget.
- [ ] **AC3 — Free-ride tier.** Every non-acting eligible player automatically receives 50% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board) with no prompt to decline, spending no action point and no coins. This is also the fallback when "join fully" is unaffordable. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Isolation, determinism & persistence.** The acting player's reward and all shared decks are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback decisions; decisions for N>2 are resolved independently per seat in a deterministic order with no additional RNG draws; a pending piggyback decision survives a save/load round-trip. Verified by tests (including a replay/equality check and a serialize→deserialize→resolve test).
- [ ] **AC5 — AI policy and human prompt.** AI seats decide whether to join fully via a deterministic strategy heuristic in `MainStreetAiStrategy`; the human seat is offered the choice to join fully (pay the cost for 100%) or keep the automatic 50% free-ride, through the existing choice/prompt plumbing. Verified by an AI-policy unit test and a scene/command-layer test for the human prompt.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md`, and any relevant PRD/scope notes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTIIL1ON006H7IL** – Shared-day phase machine: alternating MarketPhases, shared closing phases (completed)
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – When playing with AI player is credit with AI challenges (open)
- **MS-0MUQZH6BU002113D** – GitHub Pages deploy workflow (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac4, ac5, acceptance, action, actions (+372 more)
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: 0muvupwhd0032cu4, acting, action, actionbudget, actions (+301 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, acting, action, actions, active (+283 more)

# Extract shared closing presentation primitive

## Goal

Collapse the duplicated single-player and competitive end-of-turn presentation into one reusable primitive so the two flows cannot drift (absorbs `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Single-player and competitive closings are driven by one shared presentation path; `finishTurnPresentation` and `presentCompetitiveClosing` no longer duplicate the income/incident/end-of-turn/advance logic.
- Single-player behaviour is behaviourally unchanged (existing turn-flow tests pass without modification).

Ambient wander layer for the street (parent MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pedestrians wander the street: figures walk with continuous motion within the street area (below the HUD, over the street/road band, not overlapping the market/HUD panels or leaving the playfield); the layer is parented to the street container so it pans and clips with the street view.

- Layer lifecycle: create/update/resize/destroy are wired to the scene lifecycle; silhouettes use one shared runtime-generated Phaser graphic texture (`g.generateTexture`) with no new art assets.
- Accessibility and non-rendering modes unchanged: Reduced Motion and replay/headless modes perform no pedestrian rendering; every step is defensive so a throwing layer can never stall the turn.
- Tests: a rendering/bounds test of the wander bounds and a unit test of presentation-RNG isolation; the existing determinism tests remain green.

Live population reconciliation against the HUD reputation value (parent MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Population updates live with reputation: while a turn is in progress a reputation gain fades a figure in and a loss fades a figure out, so the on-street count always matches the HUD reputation value.
- Reconcile, do not rebuild: a reputation change adds/removes only the delta figures; repeated changes in one turn do not thrash the layer.
- The refresh is triggered from the same path that updates the HUD reputation counter (`animateHudValueChanges` / renderer HUD `repX`), via an animator-context accessor.
- Accessibility and non-rendering modes unchanged: Reduced Motion and replay/headless modes skip the change; no gameplay RNG is drawn; the live refresh never mutates game state or the transcript.

# Intake Brief: Upgrade-deck composition lever — raise level-2 capstone reachability

**Work item:** MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W · `feature` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 (Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption in greedy Monte Carlo)
**Producer decisions:** Option (b) — per-card market weight / draw-weight column; Q2(a) — regenerate `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` after change.

## Headline

Add a per-card draw-weight mechanism to the upgrade-deck so that level-2 capstone upgrades and their level-1 prerequisite chain appear more frequently in the market, making the expensive-tier progression reachable in the canonical greedy Monte Carlo profile.

## Problem statement

The four level-2 capstone upgrades (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`) achieve only 0–2.8% M1 pick rate because the binding constraint is co-occurrence: the market draws at most one upgrade per turn from a 78-card deck (39 templates × 2 copies), and a capstone is only purchasable when its parent business is already at level 1. Card-data-only cost tuning (MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4) could not solve this — even aggressive cost cuts (level-1 cost 200, level-2 cost 400) produced identical adoption.

## Users

- **Player** — wants a realistic path to invest in favourite businesses at late-game tier (e.g. "My Diner is doing well — should I push it to a full Restaurant?"). The most powerful upgrades should be attainable through intended progression.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the two-step upgrade chain to function as designed, demonstrably reachable in simulation, without weakening the chain or breaking difficulty balance.
- **Developer** — wants a small, measurable engine change with clean before/after Monte Carlo evidence.

User story: *As a player who has advanced my Bakery to level 1 with Grand Patisserie, I want the Grand Bakehouse card to appear in the market frequently enough that I can realistically purchase it, so that late-game investment in favourite businesses pays off.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Capstone reachability.** All four level-2 capstones reach **≥5% M1** on the canonical greedy/Medium profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 turns), with commit-stamped before/after Monte Carlo evidence.
- **Level-1 adoption rises.** Level-1 prerequisite adoption measurably increases versus the MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 after-state baseline.
- **US-19 preserved.** `requiredLevel: 1` on all four capstones; `canPurchaseUpgrade()` level equality unchanged; the two-step chain remains structurally valid.
- **Ladder preserved.** Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ordering retained; Medium win-rate within ±0.05 of the pre-change baseline.
- **Tests pass.** New deck/weight rule is covered by tests; full project test suite is green.

## Constraints

- **Draw-weight mechanism (producer-approved).** Add a per-card draw-weight column (option b from the original proposal) applied at market refill time, **not** a raw copies increase. This avoids RNG-stream contamination from `shuffleArray` Fisher–Yates (which consumes `n-1` RNG calls per shuffle in `core/src/card-system/Deck.ts`), preserving clean before/after attribution.
- **Preserve US-19** (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md`): level-2 upgrades keep `requiredLevel: 1`; the two-step chain is unchanged.
- **Market composition invariants.** Respect `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS` and the absolute ≥1-business rule in `refillSingleRowMarket`.
- **Baseline regeneration.** Producer approved regeneration of `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` (greedy + banking-greedy blocks) via `npx vite-node src/scripts/generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts` once the deck rule is in place, with before/after evidence commit-stamped. The guardrail test's drift-report-then-ask operator-approval requirement is satisfied by this explicit approval.
- **No card-stat changes.** This item touches deck/market mechanics only, not card stats or costs.

## Existing state

- Upgrade deck: 39 templates × 2 copies = 78 cards.
- Market: at most 1 upgrade per turn drawn from the 78-card deck.
- Prior cost tuning (MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4): level-1 costs 700→400/900→500, level-2 costs 900/1400/1400/1400→700/1000/1000/1000 → capstones still at 0–2.8% M1.
- Aggressive variant (level-1 cost 200, level-2 cost 400) → **identical** adoption, proving cost is not the binding constraint.
- Root cause: a capstone can only be bought when (a) parent is at level 1 AND (b) the capstone card is on the market. Across 200 runs, only 0–1 runs had both conditions satisfied.

## Reusable existing mechanisms

- **Bias-aware refill path (precedent).** `refillSingleRowMarket(state, relevance?)` already accepts a `MarketRelevanceBias { bias, synergyTypes }` and, when active, draws relevant cards with probability `bias` (see `isMarketCardRelevant`); the Investor free re-roll (`useFreeMarketReroll`, MS-0MTISBYLS009936W) uses this. The new upgrade `drawWeight` mechanism should mirror that style — an optional, refill-time-only selection bias that falls back to the existing random draw when no weights are declared. Note the existing bias path does **not** currently cover the upgrade family: `drawUpgrade` is a plain `decks.upgrade.pop()`, so the upgrade weight needs its own weighted selection.
- **CSV column plumbing.** `marketRelevanceBias` is read from `src/card-data.csv` into the staff template in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` and is optional on the card type (`MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`). `drawWeight` should follow exactly this pattern (numeric column; absent → baseline weight `1`).
- **Template spread into deck.** `createUpgradeDeck` copies templates (one card per template per copy), so a `drawWeight` field set on the template is automatically present on every deck card.

## Desired change

Implement a per-card draw-weight system: add a `drawWeight` column to the card data (or equivalent mechanism) so that upgrade-deck templates belonging to chain-relevant upgrades (the four capstones and their level-1 prerequisites) are drawn with higher probability at market refill time. The mechanism should:

1. Apply weights during market refill (in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` or `MainStreetStateSetup.ts`), not by changing deck composition at game start.
2. Preserve the `shuffleArray` call count to avoid RNG-stream contamination — i.e., the deck remains 78 cards; weights influence selection without altering deck size.
3. Target weights that produce a meaningful increase in capstone visibility without dominating the market (proposed: capstone templates weight 3–4×, level-1 prerequisite templates weight 2× relative to baseline weight 1).
4. Produce before/after Monte Carlo evidence on the canonical profile.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — add a `drawWeight` column (default `1`) for the eight chain-relevant upgrade templates (four level-1 prerequisites + four level-2 capstones).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — the upgrade-template mapping (`upgTemplates`) lists fields explicitly; read `drawWeight` here so the value reaches the card.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — add the optional `drawWeight?: number` field to `UpgradeCard` (staff already carry the analogous `marketRelevanceBias`).
- `src/MainStreetCardsDecks.ts` — `createUpgradeDeck` spreads the template (`{ ...template, id: \`${template.id}-${c}\` }`), so a template `drawWeight` propagates to every deck card automatically; only touch this file if weight-aware ordering is derived at deck-build time.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — market refill; the weighted upgrade selection belongs in `drawUpgrade` / `refillSingleRowMarket`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — `setupMainStreetGame` / `refillSingleRowMarket`; read for RNG/shuffle integration.
- `core/src/card-system/Deck.ts` — `shuffleArray`; read-only reference for RNG stream semantics.
- `tests/main-street/upgrades.test.ts` — existing `requiredLevel` enforcement and level-2 capstone coverage (e.g. Luxury Retreat); extend for the new weight rule.
  - *Correction:* the previously predicted `tests/main-street/level2-upgrade-chain.test.ts` does **not** exist in this repository.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` — baseline regeneration (producer-approved).
- `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` — regenerate via the baseline script (producer-approved Q2(a)).

## Related work

- MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 — card-data-only tuning attempt; 0–2.8% M1 for capstones; now blocked (escalated to this item).
- MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance (source item; blocked).
- MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns and economy re-tune (completed).

## Assumptions

- A draw-weight applied at refill time (rather than copies change) can produce a sufficient increase in capstone visibility without breaking market composition invariants.
- The 200-seed canonical profile provides adequate resolution for the ≥5% target.
- Weights in card-data.csv are simple numeric multipliers (e.g., `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`), applied as a factor against the baseline weight for each template.

## Risks

- **Insufficient weight increase.** If even 3–4× weights don't lift capstones to ≥5% M1, a larger weight factor or alternative lever (option 1: copies increase, with RNG-shift control) may be needed. *Mitigation:* iterate weights empirically with Monte Carlo runs; document the weight vs. M1 curve.
- **Market composition drift.** Increasing upgrade visibility could crowd out non-upgrade market cards, affecting the ≥1-business invariant. *Mitigation:* the weight applies only to upgrade templates within the upgrade slot; existing market slot invariants are preserved.
- **RNG attribution.** Even with a refill-time weight, if the upgrade deck is shuffled before the staff deck, some RNG-stream contamination persists. *Mitigation:* the weight mechanism avoids changing deck size, so the Fisher–Yates call count is identical. **Note:** `drawUpgrade` currently consumes **zero** RNG calls (`decks.upgrade.pop()`), whereas any weighted selection consumes at least one `state.rng()` call, so the refill stream shifts after the first upgrade draw even with the deck size unchanged. A same-shift control run (weights present but all set to `1`) is therefore required for clean attribution — deck-size preservation alone is not sufficient.
- **Scope creep.** Other zero-adoption upgrades (`upg-museum`, `upg-dental-clinic` with rare parents) invite broader changes. *Mitigation:* keep them out of scope; log as separate work items if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — which lever to implement?** — **Answer (operator): (b)** Per-card market weight / draw-weight column. Source: producer decision, session herdr-1791457852-3011912-17842.
- **Q2 — RNG-stream contamination concern (from option 1 analysis).** — **Answer (design): Apply weight at refill time, not via copies increase.** This preserves the 78-card deck size and the `shuffleArray` call count, keeping the RNG stream identical for clean before/after attribution. Source: producer design constraints.
- **Q3 — baseline regeneration.** — **Answer (operator): (a)** Approved regenerating `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` (greedy + banking-greedy blocks) once the new deck rule is in place. The guardrail test's drift-report-then-ask operator-approval requirement is satisfied. Source: producer decision, same session.

# Intake Brief: Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies, staff relationships and upgrade chains (MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**
**Producer decisions (2026-10-07, interactive): Q1 = A (docs/tooling artefacts); Q2 = B (named three + community-space extension); Q3 = A (committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard).** See Appendix.

## Problem statement

The repo already generates a deterministic Mermaid flowchart of the storyline
graph (`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`,
with a JSON manifest and a `--check` drift guard), but no other card dataset is
visualised. Designers, reviewers and new contributors must reconstruct card
synergies, staff coverage, upgrade chains and community-space relationships by
reading 174 CSV rows. Generating the same class of deterministic Mermaid
diagram for these datasets makes each relationship legible at a glance and
keeps the pictures drift-guarded against `src/card-data.csv`.

## Users

- **Content designer / producer** — sees at a glance which cards share a synergy,
  which staff can serve which businesses, and how upgrade chains branch and gate.
  - *"As a designer, I want a Mermaid diagram of card synergies, so I can check
    that every synergy type has a healthy cluster of cards without reading the CSV."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of staff coverage, so I can spot uncovered
    business types or overly broad staff."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of upgrade chains, so I can see the two-step
    level-1 → level-2 branches and their gates."*
- **Reviewer / balancer** — trusts the committed diagrams because a drift guard
  fails when they fall out of sync with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **New contributor / developer** — uses the diagrams as an entry point to the
  card model, alongside `card-catalog.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Diagram generator CLI.** A new dev-only npm script (e.g. `npm run
   docs:diagrams`) generates Mermaid from `src/card-data.csv` through the typed
   card model under `vite-node`, supporting `--diagram
   <synergies|staff|upgrades|community-spaces|all>` (default `all`), `--format
   mermaid|json` (default `mermaid`), `--out <path>` and `--check` (drift guard:
   exit `1` on drift, `0` when up to date). Verified by unit tests that invoke
   the CLI and assert its exit codes and output.
2. **Committed artefacts & drift guard.** Four deterministic Mermaid artefacts
   are committed under `docs/main-street/` — `card-synergies.mmd`,
   `staff-relationships.mmd`, `upgrade-chains.mmd`,
   `community-space-relationships.mmd` — and a Vitest drift guard regenerates
   each from `src/card-data.csv` and fails when the committed file differs
   byte-for-byte. The existing `storyline-graph.mmd` drift guard continues to pass.
3. **Card synergy diagram content.** Shows every business and community-space
   card and all six synergy types (Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
   Entertainment, Health), with an edge per card↔synergy membership so cards that
   can chain adjacency bonuses are identifiable. Verified by unit tests asserting
   the exact node set plus edges for representative multi-synergy cards (e.g.
   `biz-cafe` → Food + Culture; `cs-public-art` → Culture + Entertainment) and
   that all six synergy types appear.
4. **Staff relationship diagram content.** Shows every staff card, each synergy
   type and named business it may serve (`allowedBusinessTypes`, resolved through
   the existing `getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff` / `staffMatchesBusiness`
   helpers), and the specialization-skill catalog from `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`
   (categories and skills). Verified by unit tests asserting representative staff
   edges (e.g. `staff-health-safety` → Health only; `staff-chef` →
   Cafe/Diner/Delicatessen/Food) and that every catalog skill appears.
5. **Upgrade chain diagram content.** Shows each upgradeable business/community
   space as a chain root plus each applicable upgrade, ordered by
   `requiredLevel`/`maxLevel` and labelled with `newDisplayName`, so level-1
   branches and the level-2 gate are visible. Verified by unit tests asserting the
   four level-2 chains (e.g. Bakery → Patisserie / Bread Factory → Grand
   Bakehouse) and that a level-2 upgrade is only shown after a level-1 step.
6. **Community-space diagram content.** Shows each of the eight community-space
   cards, its synergy types and any community-space upgrade (`targetBusiness`),
   including ongoing cost/buff fields where set. Verified by unit tests asserting
   all eight cards and their types.
7. **Determinism & safety.** Two builds from the same CSV are deeply equal, output
   is sorted and contains no timestamp/RNG/wall-clock input, the generator adds no
   runtime dependency (dev tooling only), and Mermaid remains the source of truth
   (artefacts are never hand-edited). Verified by unit tests.
8. **Documentation.** A new `docs/main-street/card-diagrams.md` documents every
   diagram (what it shows, how to read it) and the regeneration command, and
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and
   `src/README.md` link to it. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
9. **Tests, build and full suite.** `npm run build` succeeds and the full project
   test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Mermaid is the source of truth.** The committed `.mmd` files are generated
  artefacts; never hand-edited. `src/card-data.csv` is the data source.
- **No new runtime dependency.** The generator is dev tooling only, mirroring
  `storylines:graph`; nothing enters the game bundle.
- **Determinism.** Sorted node/edge order, no RNG, timestamps or wall-clock input;
  byte-identical on re-run.
- **Read-only over data.** Do not change the card model, CSV schema/column order,
  or gameplay data; consume the existing typed getters
  (`getBusinessTemplates`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates`, `getUpgradeTemplates`,
  `getStaffCardTemplates`) and `MainStreetStaffSkills`.
- **Rendering is out of scope.** SVG/PNG rendering of Mermaid stays with
  `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`; this item commits `.mmd` (and offers `--format json` on
  demand only).
- **Scope guard.** Additional diagram domains beyond the four named (plus the
  already-existing storyline graph) are separate work items; record them rather
  than absorbing them here.
- **UK English** in all generated labels and documentation.
- **No CHANGELOG.md edits** (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Generator precedent.** `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` builds a
  deterministic manifest and renders Mermaid; `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts`
  is the `vite-node` entry (`npm run storylines:graph`); `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`
  holds the existing byte-for-byte drift guard.
- **Typed getters.** `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` exposes
  `getBusinessTemplates`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates`, `getEventTemplates`,
  `getUpgradeTemplates`, `getStaffCardTemplates` (re-exported via
  `src/MainStreetCards.ts`).
- **Data.** `src/card-data.csv` — 174 rows: 31 business, 39 upgrade, 25 staff,
  8 community-space, 71 event. Synergy types: Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
  Entertainment, Health.
- **Synergies.** `BusinessCard`/`CommunitySpaceCard` carry `synergyTypes`,
  `synergyCoinBonus`, `synergyRepBonus`; staff `skill-network`/`skill-tech-guru`
  modify adjacency behaviour.
- **Staff.** `staff.allowedBusinessTypes` mixes synergy types and specific
  business names (e.g. `Cafe|Diner|Food|Delicatessen`); resolved by
  `getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff` / `staffMatchesBusiness`. Specialization
  skills live in `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` (category + effect).
- **Upgrades.** `upgrade.targetBusiness` + `upgrade.requiredLevel` + business
  `maxLevel`; `upgrade.newDisplayName` names the upgraded form. Four level-2
  upgrades gate on a level-1 parent (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`,
  `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`).
- **Community spaces.** Eight cards with `synergyTypes` and community-space
  upgrades (e.g. `upg-orchard` → Community Garden).
- **Docs.** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` catalogues cards; `storylines.md`
  documents the storyline graph tooling and links `storyline-graph.mmd`;
  `src/README.md` references the scripts; there is **no** `card-diagrams.md` and
  no diagram for synergies/staff/upgrades/community spaces.

## Desired change

1. Add a deterministic diagram generator (`src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` + CLI)
   that builds, for the four domains, a node/edge manifest from the typed card
   model and renders Mermaid, reusing the storyline-graph conventions
   (deterministic ordering, `--check`, `--format`, `--out`).
2. Commit the four `.mmd` artefacts under `docs/main-street/`.
3. Add an npm script (`docs:diagrams`) and a Vitest drift guard for each
   artefact.
4. Document the diagrams and the regeneration workflow, and cross-link from
   `card-catalog.md`, `storylines.md` and `src/README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` — **new**: manifest builders and Mermaid renderers for synergies, staff, upgrades and community spaces (deterministic; mirrors `storyline-graph.ts`).
- `src/scripts/card-diagrams-cli.ts` — **new** `vite-node` CLI entry with `--diagram`, `--format`, `--out`, `--check`.
- `package.json` — add the `docs:diagrams` script.
- `docs/main-street/card-synergies.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/staff-relationships.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/upgrade-chains.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/community-space-relationships.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/card-diagrams.md` — **new**: diagram guide + regeneration commands.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — link the diagrams.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — cross-reference the unified diagram tooling (§5/§11).
- `src/README.md` — document the new script and artefacts.
- `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` — **new**: determinism, content-correctness and drift-guard tests.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — read-only reuse of the typed getters.
- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — read-only specialization-skill catalog source.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed) — the generator/drift-guard pattern this item mirrors.
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (open) — owns Mermaid→SVG rendering; out of scope here.
- **MS-0MUYK064P0032374** — Static docs site that renders Mermaid docs at build time (open) — a future rendering surface for these artefacts.
- **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** — Visual storyline authoring editor (open, epic) — an interactive graph viewer; potential consumer of the diagram model.
- **MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY** — Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift guard (completed) — docs conventions this item follows.
- **MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN** — Synergy tooltop (completed) — established synergy-type player-facing semantics.
- **MS-0MUR9INHX001QCSE** — Track synergy diversity (G4/HHI) and placement dominance post-rebalance (open) — analytical use of the same synergy data.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** — Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption in greedy Monte Carlo (in-progress) — the level gate visualised in the upgrade chain diagram.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MULWEEE8007J2TB** – Fix Accountant refreshCostDiscount value to ×100 scale (completed)
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** – Competitive state model: per-player resources, owner-tagged street (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — matched: chains, synergies, staff, upgrades, requiredlevel, maxlevel, specialization (+26 more)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: diagram, generate, graph, manifest, card, staff, upgrades (+35 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: diagram, generate, graph, manifest, card, staff, upgrades (+31 more)

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (MEDIUM).** "Any other sensible information" invites unbounded diagrams. *Mitigation:* fix the set at the four named domains plus the existing storyline graph; extra domains become separate work items.
- **Diagram readability (MEDIUM).** A 31-business synergy graph can become dense. *Mitigation:* group by synergy type (central type nodes), keep labels compact (name + id), and offer `--diagram` for per-domain output.
- **Upgrade-chain modelling (MEDIUM).** `requiredLevel` + `maxLevel` encode a graph that can branch (Bakery has two level-1 options and one level-2). *Mitigation:* model chains by `targetBusiness` + `requiredLevel`, assert the four level-2 chains explicitly in tests.
- **Staff target ambiguity (LOW).** `allowedBusinessTypes` mixes synergy types with business names. *Mitigation:* resolve through the existing helpers and distinguish node kinds in the diagram/tests.
- **Drift staleness (LOW).** Committed diagrams can diverge from the CSV. *Mitigation:* per-artefact `--check` drift guard.
- **Assumption** — "diagrams" means committed Mermaid artefacts in the docs, not an in-game viewer (Q1 = A).
- **Assumption** — the four named domains plus the community-space extension are the v1 set (Q2 = B).
- **Assumption** — `.mmd` is committed and drift-guarded; `--format json` is available on demand but not committed (Q3 = A).
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface: where do the diagrams live?** Options: (A) docs/tooling artefacts (committed `.mmd` under `docs/main-street/`, mirroring `storylines:graph`); (B) in-game player-facing Mermaid viewer; (C) both. **Recommended: (A).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — docs/tooling artefacts. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Diagram scope.** Options: (A) the three named domains only; (B) A plus a curated extension (community-space relationships and other clearly diagram-worthy data); (C) a single combined "everything" diagram. **Recommended: (B).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (B)** — named three plus the community-space extension. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Output and guarding.** Options: (A) deterministic committed `.mmd` plus a `--check` drift guard per diagram; (B) on-demand only, no committed artefacts or guard; (C) A plus rendered SVG/PNG (overlaps `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`). **Recommended: (A).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard; SVG rendering stays with `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`. Source: interactive reply.

Research note (agent, no producer input needed): the storyline generator
(`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`) is the established pattern (`--format`,
`--out`, `--check`, deterministic ordering, committed artefact + drift test);
the typed template getters for business/community-space/upgrade/staff already
exist; and no synergy/staff/upgrade/community-space diagram exists today.

by the test-first sibling item (producer answers Q1 (A), Q2 (B), Q3 (A)).

## Goal

As a content designer, I want the storyline graph shown as a committed image in
the docs, regenerated by one documented command, so I can inspect the shipped
chains without a Mermaid renderer and reviewers can trust the picture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Renderer.** A new render module/CLI (e.g. `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` + a CLI entry) renders `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` to `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg` using the already-installed Playwright Chromium and the `mermaid` JS package. *Metric: CLI produces the committed SVG; unit test on the pure render→normalise step.*

# Farm to Table is too OP

**Headline.** Retune the `evt-farm-table` (Farm-to-Table Feature) Incident
reward from **600 coins / 100 reputation** to **400 coins / 65 reputation**
(a reduction of at least one third, rounded to the nearest 5), keeping the
Restaurant Renaissance escalation strictly better than its trigger, and
validate the change against the canonical balance guardrails.

## Problem statement

The Farm-to-Table Feature Incident (`evt-farm-table`), the terminal positive
escalation of the Restaurant Renaissance storyline, awards a flat 600 coins and
100 reputation. That windfall is large enough to distort the turn economy and
makes the escalation disproportionately valuable relative to every other
Incident, including its own trigger. The producer wants the reward reduced by
at least one third.

## Users

- **Producer / balance owner** — wants positive Incident rewards that do not
  overwhelm the business economy or trivialise a run; needs an evidence-led
  retune with guardrail validation.
- **Player** — should experience Farm-to-Table as a meaningful but not
  game-deciding reward for rejecting the Popular Menu Item branch.

Example user story: *As a player who rejects Popular Menu Item and escalates
to Farm-to-Table Feature, I want a reward that feels better than the trigger
without trivialising the run.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reward retuned.** The `evt-farm-table` row in `src/card-data.csv` has
   `coinDelta = 400` and `reputationDelta = 65` (a ≥ one-third reduction from
   600/100, rounded to the nearest 5), and its `description` / `effect` text
   states the new values.
2. **Escalation invariant preserved.** The Restaurant Renaissance escalation
   remains strictly better than its trigger — `evt-farm-table`
   (`400 + 65 = 465`) > `evt-popular-menu` (`300 + 0 = 300`) — and
   `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts` passes (with an explicit value
   assertion added or updated).
3. **Generated artefacts regenerated and consistent.** `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`
   is regenerated from the CSV (`npm run storylines:graph`) and the card SVG
   plus `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` are
   regenerated (`node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`); the
   storyline drift test and card-manifest test pass.
4. **Balance guardrail evidence.** A canonical 200-seed greedy Monte Carlo run
   is performed and compared against the committed baseline via the drift
   report; the result (including the card's draw frequency and whether any
   move is within noise) and rationale are recorded in a balance evidence note
   under `docs/main-street/`. The committed baseline is **not** regenerated
   without producer approval.
5. **Documentation and tests.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Data is source of truth.** All changes are card-data changes (CSV);
  no engine-rule changes.
- **Integer economy.** Coin/reputation values are whole integers, rounded to
  the nearest 5.
- **Chain structure preserved.** `evt-farm-table` remains a terminal,
  choice-less, plain positive Incident; ids and chain links are unchanged.
- **Baseline governance.** Per the balance-guardrail drift workflow, do not
  silently regenerate `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`; report
  drift and seek producer approval before any baseline update.
- **Scope discipline.** No other card or storyline is retuned here; any further
  balance concerns become separate work items.

## Existing state

- `evt-farm-table` row in `src/card-data.csv`: `family=event`,
  `trigger=Incident`, `target=All`, `tier=5`, `coinDelta=600`,
  `reputationDelta=100`, `description` / `effect` = "Farm-to-table features
  earn 600 coins and 100 reputation.", `storylineId=storyline-restaurant`,
  terminal (no accept/reject links).
- Trigger `evt-popular-menu`: `+300` coins, `0` reputation, `hasChoices=true`,
  reject → `evt-farm-table` (accept ends the chain).
- `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts` asserts the rejected escalation is
  strictly better than the trigger.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` is drift-tested byte-for-byte
  against `src/card-data.csv` (`tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` holds generated card SVGs and
  `csv-checksum.json`; the runtime (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign`)
  compares that file's checksum with the bundled `CSV_CHECKSUM`.

## Desired change

Reduce the flat Farm-to-Table reward to 400 coins / 65 reputation, update the
card's effect/description text, regenerate the derived artefacts, and record
the balance-guardrail evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — `evt-farm-table` row: `coinDelta` 600 → 400,
  `reputationDelta` 100 → 65, and the `description` / `effect` strings.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — regenerate via
  `npm run storylines:graph` (drift-tested artefact).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` and the
  `evt-farm-table` SVG — regenerate via
  `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`.
- `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — update the stale `+600` upper-bound
  comment/reference.
- `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts` — keep/extend the explicit
  escalation value assertion.
- `docs/main-street/analysis/` — new balance evidence note (drift report +
  rationale), following the pattern of `community-space-event-repricing.md`.

## Related work

- **MS-0MTT7FC7A000AA58 — Content: New chain cards and retro-fitting**
  (completed): introduced the Restaurant Renaissance chain and its reward
  levels.
- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns and
  economy re-tune** (completed): parent economy campaign; this card's value is
  read relative to the slower payback profile.
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5 — Re-price community spaces and events relative to
  slower business payback** (task): direct precedent for an evidence-led
  incident/event reward retune, including Monte Carlo guardrail validation.
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE — Re-tune reputation sources for the slower-coin
  economy** (task): precedent for treating reputation as a balance lever.
- A `find-related` automated report (work items and repo file matches) is
  maintained on the work item description.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption.** "divide by at least 1/3rd" means *reduce by at least one
  third* (producer confirmed option A); rounding 66.67 down to 65 keeps the
  reduction ≥ one third.
- **Assumption.** The reputation reward scales with the coin reward (producer
  confirmed option A).
- **Risk.** A single low-frequency card may not move the Monte Carlo metrics
  beyond noise; the evidence note must state draw frequency and confidence
  rather than implying a measurable win-rate effect.
- **Risk.** Editing the CSV without regenerating `storyline-manifest.json`
  fails the byte-for-byte drift test; editing without regenerating the SVG
  checksum desyncs the runtime card-art regeneration path.
- **Risk (scope creep).** Other storylines/incidents may also read as
  overpowered; record those as separate work items rather than expanding this
  one.
- **Assumption.** No engine-rule change is needed — the reward is a flat
  `target=All` delta applied once.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should the reward be retuned?**
  Options: (A) reduce *by* at least 1/3 → 400 / 66 rep; (B) reduce *to* one
  third → 200 / 33 rep; (C) other.
  **Recommended:** A.
  — **Answer (producer):** "A but round to nearest 5" → **400 coins / 65
  reputation**. Source: interactive reply. Resolves the conflict with the
  `chain-content.test.ts` escalation invariant (465 > 300).
- **Q2 — Scale the reputation reward too?**
  Options: (A) scale both; (B) coins only; (C) reputation only.
  **Recommended:** A.
  — **Answer (producer):** "A". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Validation scope (balance change)?**
  Options: (A) canonical 200-seed greedy Monte Carlo guardrail run + evidence
  note; (B) data + unit/doc updates only.
  **Recommended:** A.
  — **Answer (producer):** "A". Source: interactive reply.

Open questions: none.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MURODBVT007ZJLT** – Add docs-path-drift.test.ts Vitest drift guard (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, added, also, analysis (+241 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: 0muq50i1y000b6l3, accept, added, analysis, answer (+193 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, added, also, analysis (+189 more)

# Intake Brief: Ownership-aware AI placement — do not place synergy that only benefits other players

**Work item:** MS-0MUYODDW300690KX · `bug` · `high`
**Discovered from:** observed competitive play — the AI places community spaces that anchor the human player's businesses but give the AI nothing
**Related precedent:** [MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW](MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW) (community-space scoring + business-preference penalty), [MS-0MT5X3N79002S038](MS-0MT5X3N79002S038) (competitive ownership-aware AI scoring)

## Headline

In shared-street (competitive) play the AI's placement scoring counts the synergy a card anchors for **every** neighbouring business, regardless of who owns it. A community space that only boosts an opponent's businesses can therefore score positive, and the AI spends coins and pays an ongoing running cost to enrich a rival. The competitive placement score must be ownership-aware: credit only the synergy the acting AI gains, and subtract (or refuse) the synergy it hands to other players, so the AI places a card only when **its own benefit exceeds the benefit it confers on others**.

## Problem statement

`scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` (used by both the single-player and competitive spend chains) computes a community space's value from `neighbourSynergyGain`, which sums the marginal synergy income added to **all** adjacent businesses with no owner filter. In single-player there is only the acting seat, so this is correct. In competitive/shared-street play (`state.ownerTaggedGrid` present, `isCompetitiveMode(state) === true`) the grid holds businesses owned by the acting AI **and** by other seats. When the AI considers a slot adjacent to an opponent's matching-synergy business — but not its own — `neighbourSynergyGain` still returns a positive number, so the community space can clear `COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY` and be bought/played. The AI then pays the placement cost and the `ongoingCost × horizon` drain to increase a rival's income.

The same blind spot applies to the other direction for any card: `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` measure only the placed card's own income + synergy and never account for the synergy the placement anchors for neighbouring **opponent** businesses. The seed's general rule — "only place cards (any cards) where the benefits to the AI are greater than to other players" — therefore is not met by the current competitive scoring.

Ownership is already modelled (`getSlotOwnerId` / `ownerTaggedGrid`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`) and used elsewhere in the competitive AI (`countOwnSynergyMatches`, `competitiveUpgradeTargets`), so this is a fix to the scoring path, not a new system.

## Users

- **Human player (seat 0) vs AI opponents** — a shared-street competitive game should not be handed an economic gift by an AI that anchors the human's businesses for free.
  - *"As the human player, I want the AI to compete for its own advantage, so my businesses don't get free synergy the AI paid for."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants competitive AI behaviour to follow the intended principle (own benefit ≥ benefit to others), with measurable before/after evidence and no change to single-player balance baselines.
  - *"As the producer, I want competitive AI placements to be ownership-aware so the AI plays to win rather than boosting opponents."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ownership-aware community-space value (competitive).** In competitive mode, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` (or a competitive variant invoked by `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore`) counts neighbour synergy only for slots owned by the acting player. Synergy anchored for a business owned by any other seat is not credited and is subtracted from the placement score, so the score reflects `own gain − opponent gain`.
2. **Opponent-only community space is rejected.** A community space placed into a slot whose only positive value is synergy for another seat's business scores `≤ 0`; `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` therefore returns `false` and the greedy AI does not buy or play it (measured by a unit test constructing an opponent-owned adjacent business).
3. **Self-beneficial placements preserved.** A community space whose synergy anchors the acting AI's own businesses retains a positive score and is still chosen; a community space anchoring a mix of own and opponent businesses scores strictly less than the identical placement with only own businesses (no regression for genuine self-interest).
4. **All competitive placements charge opponent benefit.** For ordinary business placements in competitive mode, the placement score subtracts the marginal synergy income the placement anchors for neighbouring **opponent** businesses (net differential), while the acting player's own income/synergy valuation is unchanged. The eligibility gate for income-producing businesses is unchanged (they remain always eligible); the differential is reflected in how they rank against alternatives.
5. **Single-player unchanged.** With no `ownerTaggedGrid` (N=1), `scoreAction`, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` and `GreedyStrategy` produce identical scores/decisions to today; `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` pass unmodified.
6. **Determinism preserved.** The same seed + same strategy yields an identical competitive action sequence (`CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`), and no RNG is introduced into the ownership-aware scoring.
7. **Evidence captured.** Before/after competitive head-to-head evidence shows the rate of placements conferring net benefit on opponents falls (net of single-player baselines, which are unchanged), committed alongside the change.
8. **Documentation updated.** The competitive placement rule (own benefit must exceed benefit handed to other seats) is documented in the AI strategy docs and code doc-comments, including the `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` / competitive-score comments.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Scoring heuristic only — no engine or rule changes.** Reuse the existing ownership model (`getSlotOwnerId`, `ownerTaggedGrid`) and the existing synergy computation (`computeSynergyBonus`); do not change income routing, `computeSynergyBonus` semantics, or the same-type penalty.
- **Single-player paths must remain behaviourally identical** (N=1 fallback), preserving the committed Monte Carlo balance baselines (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`).
- **Preserve the existing business-preference semantics** (`COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY`, positive-score eligibility for community spaces).
- **No new randomness;** scoring stays deterministic.
- **Reputation and shared/global effects** stay valued as they are today (reputation is per-owner; only synergy-attribution changes).
- **Scope-creep risk:** widening this into a full multi-seat minimax/opponent-modelling rework, or retuning card costs, is out of scope — record follow-ups as linked work items.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `neighbourSynergyGain(grid, placed, slotIndex, bonusPerNeighbor)` sums synergy gains for every neighbour with no owner filter (lines ~180–206). `communitySpacePlacementValueAt` uses it for `neighbourIncome`; `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` is the public entry point and is called from `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` (the "competitive mirror" explicitly documented in `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md`). `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` for ordinary businesses count only `(baseIncome + projectedSynergy) × horizon − cost`. `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gates community spaces on `score > 0`.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — `getSlotOwnerId(state, slotIndex)` (owner tag with active-player fallback) and `ownerTaggedGrid`; the established ownership source used by `countOwnSynergyMatches` and `competitiveUpgradeTargets`.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `computeSynergyBonus(grid, index, bonusPerNeighbor, soldSlots, gridDims)`; the ownership-agnostic per-card synergy used by the before/after diff.
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — competitive head-to-head harness (`runCompetitiveMonteCarlo`, `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`) for before/after evidence.
- Existing competitive scoring is already ownership-aware for events (`computeCompetitiveEventValue` counts only the acting player's matching businesses) and upgrades (own slots only); placement is the remaining ownership-blind path.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` (ownership-aware scoring, `place()` fixture tagging owners), `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` (single-player community-space value), `tests/main-street/no-phantom-synergy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/same-type-synergy.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce an ownership-aware neighbour-synergy attribution helper (e.g. `neighbourSynergyGainByOwner(...)` returning `{ own, opponent }`, or an optional owner filter on `neighbourSynergyGain`), using `getSlotOwnerId(state, i)` against the acting seat.
2. Use it in the competitive placement value so a community space's `neighbourIncome` credits only the acting player's slots and subtracts (or excludes and negatively weights) opponent slots, yielding an `own − opponent` net placement value.
3. Apply the same opponent-benefit term to the ordinary business competitive scores so any placement is penalised by the synergy it anchors for opponents.
4. Keep single-player `scoreAction` / `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` on the ownership-agnostic path (all slots belong to the acting seat) so baselines do not move.
5. Add focused unit tests (own-only, opponent-only, mixed) and capture before/after competitive Monte Carlo evidence; update the AI strategy docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — add ownership-aware neighbour-synergy attribution; thread it through `communitySpacePlacementValueAt` / `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` and `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore`; keep `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gating community spaces on the ownership-aware score.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — reference only (`getSlotOwnerId`, `ownerTaggedGrid`); no change expected.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — reference only (`computeSynergyBonus`); no change expected.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — new AC1–AC3 tests: opponent-owned adjacent business makes an opponent-only community space ineligible; own-only placement stays positive; mixed placement scores below own-only.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` — confirm single-player scores are unchanged (AC5).
- `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` — confirm `GreedyStrategy` decisions unchanged (AC5).
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — reference for the competitive harness; add/extend a report to capture opponent-benefit placement rate if needed.
- `src/scripts/balance/community-space-placement-report.ts` — reference/extension point for before/after evidence.
- `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the competitive ownership-aware placement rule (own benefit must exceed opponent benefit).
- `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md` — note that the competitive mirror is now ownership-aware.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW** (completed) — *AI uses community space cards too much.* Introduced `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement`, the neighbour-anchoring value and `COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY`; this item fixes the ownership blind spot left in that competitive mirror.
- **MS-0MT5X3N79002S038** (completed) — *Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free scoring for shared-street play.* Established the competitive scoring/enumeration layer this change extends; its AC1 ("ownership-aware scoring") currently covers resources/own businesses but not the synergy handed to opponents.
- **MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ** (completed) — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution.* Established per-owner income accrual on the shared street (why opponent synergy gain is a real benefit to a rival).
- **MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y** (completed) — *AI should not use Community Favour as much.* Same family of AI-heuristic corrections.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (from seed):** the target is competitive/shared-street play ("other players"); single-player has no opponent and must not change.
- **Assumption (from seed):** the general principle applies to *any* card, so ordinary business placements also subtract opponent benefit; the observed, most damaging case is community spaces.
- **Assumption:** "benefit to other players" from a placement means the marginal synergy income credited to their businesses; reputation/global events are out of scope (valued as today).
- **Balance risk:** subtracting opponent benefit could suppress legitimate business placements in tight shared-street configurations. Mitigation: keep own income/base value intact and subtract only the anchored opponent synergy; verify against the competitive harness that AI scores/win rate do not regress materially.
- **Baseline risk:** touching a shared helper could leak into single-player. Mitigation: explicit N=1 fallback and unchanged single-player tests (`community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts`, `ai-strategy.test.ts`, Monte Carlo baseline guardrail).
- **Determinism risk:** adding ownership lookups must not introduce ordering/RNG variance. Mitigation: AC6 determinism test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a full opponent-modelling/minimax rewrite, or cost retuning, is out of scope — record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope — which seats):** "Is this competitive (multi-seat shared-street) only, or also single-player?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "Competitive only. The seed says 'the player' and 'other players', and single-player has no opponent; `isCompetitiveMode` and `ownerTaggedGrid` already distinguish the two. Single-player behaviour must remain identical." Source: self-research of `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` (`isCompetitiveMode`, `getSlotOwnerId`) and `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md`. Accepted: competitive-only change with N=1 fallback.
- **Q2 (scope — card families):** "Which placements must be ownership-aware — community spaces only, or all cards?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "All cards, per the seed's 'any cards'. The scoring change is generalised, but community spaces are the observed defect and the primary acceptance test; ordinary businesses keep their own income and are penalised only by the opponent synergy they anchor." Source: seed description; `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` inspection. Accepted.
- **Q3 (objective function):** "Is the AI objective 'ignore opponent benefit' or 'maximise own benefit − opponent benefit'?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "'Own benefit − opponent benefit', per 'benefits to the AI are greater than to other players'. A placement that helps an opponent more than the AI should score ≤ 0 and be rejected for community spaces." Source: seed description; existing `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` `score > 0` gate. Accepted.
- **Q4 (verification):** "What proves the fix?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "Focused unit tests (own-only positive, opponent-only rejected, mixed scores below own-only) plus before/after competitive Monte Carlo evidence and the unchanged single-player suite/baselines." Source: `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` fixtures; `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`. Accepted.
- **No producer-blocking open questions.** The seed plus existing ownership infrastructure make the intent clear; assumptions above are recorded for producer confirmation at the review gate.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUOSUMNK000QZ62** – Update documentation for Investor card and mechanics (blocked)
- **MS-0MUV9P89G0061SRA** – Prevent players from selling, closing, or upgrading businesses they do not own (open)
- **MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4** – Turns do not bank when playing against AI (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `core/docs/the-build/concept-evaluation.md` — matched: benefit, benefits, cards, general, place, player, players, provide, should, space, synergies, where

# Producer rework — pedestrians walk roads and enter shops

The manual producer audit on the parent (MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E, 2026-10-07) rejected the completed pedestrian layer. The free-wander crowd is not the intended behaviour. The producer's verbatim feedback:

> Rejected by manual review. The people should walk on the roads only, unless they are entering a shop to spend money. During the players turn and in the end turn phase if necessary people will walk "into" shops where they will spend their money during the reputation income phase of the end turn. Once in the shop they will stay there. At the start of a new turn they willbe cleared from the screen and a new set of people will wander onto the street from all four corners of the block. They will walk along the roads until they choose to enter one of the occupied cells. By the time it gets to the reputation income phase at least 25% will be in occupied cells. When increasing the money for the shop they persons in the shop will be where the money comes from.

## Scope

Rework `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` (and the reputation phase sourcing in `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`) so that:

1. Figures walk on the road bands only (never across business cells), entering a business cell only to visit a shop.
2. Figures may enter an occupied cell (a player-owned business) to spend money; once inside, they stay.
3. At the start of a new turn, all figures are cleared and a fresh set wander onto the street from the four corners of the block.
4. The reputation income phase sources each business's coins from the figures inside that business (falling back to a street anchor, never the HUD counter).
5. By the reputation income phase at least 25% of live figures are inside occupied cells.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Figures are constrained to road bands; pure helper + behaviour test assert a wandering figure never leaves the road band (its centre stays within a road band, accounting for silhouette half-size).
2. Figures can enter an occupied shop cell and remain there; a pure/behaviour test asserts entry into a business cell only when it is an occupied shop, and that entered figures stay put.
3. Population resets at turn start: figures are cleared and respawned from the four block corners; behaviour test asserts clear-then-respawn and corner origins.
4. Reputation income is sourced from figures inside shops: `dissolveIntoCoins` maps each business's coin flight to a figure inside that business, with a street-anchor fallback (never the HUD counter). Unit test asserts the source is a shop occupant and the credited total is unchanged.
5. Enforced shop occupancy: at reputation-phase time at least 25% of live figures are inside occupied cells (deterministic enforcement); unit test asserts the ratio.
6. Reduced Motion + replay/headless exemptions unchanged; no gameplay RNG consumption; presentation-only failures swallowed.
7. Documentation (`docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`) updated for the road/shop behaviour.
8. Build + full suite green.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — road-band walking, occupied-cell entry, turn-start reset, 25% enforcement, shop-sourced dissolve.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — reputation phase sources coins from shop occupants.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — hook the new-turn clear/respawn.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — new constants.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — documentation.
- `tests/main-street/` — new/updated tests.

## Assumptions

- "Occupied cell" = a street slot holding a player-owned business (`state.streetGrid[i]` present). Competitive per-seat populations remain out of scope until MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I lands; the human seat's businesses are used.
- Roads are the drawn road bands from `mapRoadBands` / `streetViewportRect`.
- "At least 25%" is enforced deterministically at reputation-phase time (presentation-only) rather than left to chance.
- Figures enter shops chosen at random among occupied cells; if no occupied cells exist, figures keep walking the roads and the coins fall back to the street anchor.
data.title: Rework pedestrians: road-walking and shop-entry reputation source

# Producer polish pass 2 — pedestrian behaviour refinements

Second round of producer feedback on the reputation crowd (MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E). The producer's verbatim follow-up:

> The people only walk down the middle of the road, they should walk on either side of the middle. They should not "teleport" to the occupoed cells, but they should walk deliberately to them. They should not dissappear and reset when a card is taken or played, but continue from where they were. They should not simply dissappear at the end of the day but walk "off screen" at the end of the block, during the end phase.

## Scope

Refine `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` (and the end-of-turn hook) so that:

1. Figures walk offset from the road centre-line — on one side of the road or the other — not down the middle.
2. Entering a shop is a deliberate walk: the figure moves continuously from the road to the shop and only becomes "inside" on arrival. No snapping/teleporting (including the reputation-phase 25% top-up, which must direct figures to *walk* in, not teleport).
3. The crowd persists across street rebuilds (a card being played or the street refreshing): figures keep their positions, lanes and modes instead of being destroyed and respawned from the corners.
4. At the end of the turn (end phase) the crowd does not vanish in place: figures that are not spending walk **off the block** (off-screen) during the income show; the rest walk deliberately into occupied shops. A fresh set still enters from the block corners at the start of the next turn.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Road lanes.** Figures walk on either side of the road centre-line (a per-figure perpendicular lane offset). A pure/behaviour test asserts a walking figure's centre is offset from the nearest road centre-line by the lane offset (and still lies on the road band), and that both sides are used.
2. **Deliberate shop entry.** `stepPedestrianFigure` moves a figure continuously toward the shop target; the figure is only marked `inside` on arrival. A test asserts a single step does not move the figure to the shop centre (no teleport) and that repeated steps bring it inside.
3. **Crowd persists across rebuilds.** `attachToStreet` re-creates the layer around the existing figures without respawning them; a test asserts figure positions/modes are unchanged across an `attachToStreet` that follows normal walking.
4. **End-of-turn walk-off.** `beginEndOfTurn()` (hooked into the end-of-turn presentation) directs at least 25% of the crowd to walk into occupied shops and sends the rest walking off the block; tests assert non-shoppers move to/beyond the block bounds (removed when off-screen) and that `startNewTurn()` then clears leftovers and spawns a fresh corner-entering crowd.
5. **Income source.** The reputation phase still sources coins from figures inside occupied shops (falling back to in-transit figures, then a street anchor — never the HUD counter); the credited total is unchanged.
6. **Exemptions & safety.** Reduced Motion/replay exemptions, no gameplay-RNG consumption and defensive non-blocking behaviour are preserved.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` and `src/scenes/README.md` updated for lanes, deliberate entry, persistence and the end-of-turn walk-off.
8. **Build + full suite green.**

## Assumptions

- "Walk on either side of the middle" = a fixed perpendicular offset from the road centre-line (a lane), with each figure keeping a side for a segment and re-choosing on turn.
- "Off screen at the end of the block" = walk toward and past the nearest boundary of the road-network bounding box (`networkBounds`), then the layer removes the figure once it is clear of the block.
- The 25% shop minimum is still a target, achieved by figures walking in (inside or in transit by the reputation sub-phase), never by teleporting.
data.title: Pedestrian polish: road lanes, deliberate shop entry, crowd persistence, end-of-turn walk-off
