# Producer feedback — in-shop pedestrians should spread across the cell

Producer feedback on the reputation crowd (MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E):

> When people are in the occupied cells they should spread randomly across the cell, not all go to the exact same spot.

## Scope

Today a figure entering a shop walks to the shop's exact centre (`beginShopEntry` sets `destX/destY` to the slot centre), so every shopper in the same cell converges on one point. Give each figure its own random destination **inside** the shop cell, so a crowd in one business spreads across it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A figure entering an occupied cell walks to a per-figure random point inside the cell (inset so the silhouette stays within the cell), not the exact centre.
2. Multiple figures assigned to the same shop receive different destinations (spread), and each walks to its own spot and stays there.
3. Coverage: a unit test asserts the entry destination is inside the cell and differs across figures; a behaviour test asserts figures in the same shop end up at distinct interior positions.
4. No teleporting, exemptions and determinism behaviour are unchanged; build + full suite green.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — `occupiedShops` (expose cell interior bounds), `beginShopEntry` (random interior destination).
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-layer.test.ts` — spread tests.

# Pedestrians should seek the nearest occupied cell (and pick up mid-turn fills)

Producer feedback on the reputation crowd (MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E):

> If a cell is filled during the turn then the people do not walk to it, they should. In addition, people should always walk to the nearest occupied cell.

## Problem

Pedestrians currently wander the roads and only enter a shop when their random walk happens to bring them within the shop's capture zone; a cell filled mid-turn (the player places a business) is therefore rarely visited. The producer wants pedestrians to **actively head for the nearest occupied cell**, retargeting when a new (nearer) cell is filled during the turn.

## Scope

Change the walking behaviour so a walking figure continuously resolves the **nearest occupied cell** (by distance), walks the road network toward that cell's entry intersection (greedy road-graph pathing), and enters it on arrival. Retarget when a nearer cell appears. No teleporting; road-lane walking, exemptions and determinism are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A walking figure resolves the nearest occupied cell and records it as its target (`nearestShop`); a test asserts the target is the nearest of several occupied cells.
2. Figures walk the road network toward the target cell's entry intersection (`nearestNodeToShop` + greedy `chooseNextToward`) and enter it on arrival; a behaviour test drives a figure into the nearest cell and asserts it becomes `inside`.
3. A cell filled mid-turn is picked up: a test adds a nearer occupied cell and asserts a walking figure retargets to it.
4. Nearest targeting is pure/headless-testable and deterministic; no gameplay RNG; reduced-motion/replay and defensive behaviour unchanged.
5. Build + full suite green.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — `nearestShop`, `nearestNodeToShop`, greedy `chooseNextToward`, updated `stepPedestrianFigure`.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-layer.test.ts` — nearest-targeting and mid-turn-fill tests.
data.title: Pedestrians seek the nearest occupied cell (including mid-turn fills)

# Add ownership-aware placement scoring tests

**Work item:** Parent AC1–AC6 (test coverage) — test-first, expected red until the implementation lands.
**Parent:** MS-0MUYODDW300690KX (AI should not place synergies that only benefit the player)

## Summary

Add focused unit tests that pin the ownership-aware competitive placement contract **before** the implementation lands (test-first). The tests construct competitor-owned adjacent businesses using the existing owner-tagging fixture (`place(...)`) and assert the `own − opponent` net placement value, the community-space eligibility gate, and that single-player scoring is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Opponent-only community space is rejected.** With an adjacent business owned by another seat, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement(...)` returns `<= 0` and `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy` does not buy or play the card.
- **Self-beneficial placement preserved.** A community space whose synergy anchors the acting AI's own adjacent business still scores `> 0` and is selected.
- **Mixed placement is discounted.** A community space anchoring a mix of own and opponent businesses scores strictly less than the identical placement adjacent to only own businesses.
- **Ordinary business differential.** In competitive mode, an ordinary business placement's score is reduced by the marginal synergy it anchors for neighbouring opponent businesses; the acting player's own income/synergy valuation is unchanged and the action remains eligible.
- **Single-player unchanged.** `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` pass unmodified (no `ownerTaggedGrid`, N=1).
- **Determinism.** Same seed + `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy` yields an identical competitive action sequence.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` with a community-space fixture and an owner-tagged neighbour setup.
2. Add own-only, opponent-only and mixed scoring cases.
3. Add the ordinary-business opponent-benefit differential case.
4. Add the N=1 single-player regression assertion and a competitive determinism test.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first; runs red until the implementation item lands).

## Deliverables

- New/updated unit tests covering parent AC1–AC6.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`

# Implement ownership-aware placement scoring

**Work item:** Parent AC1–AC6 (implementation).
**Parent:** MS-0MUYODDW300690KX (AI should not place synergies that only benefit the player)

## Summary

Make competitive placement scoring ownership-aware. Introduce a neighbour-synergy attribution helper that splits anchored synergy by owner (`getSlotOwnerId` against the acting seat) and thread it through the competitive placement value so a placement is scored as `own gain − opponent gain`. Single-player keeps the existing ownership-agnostic path so its baselines do not move.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Ownership-aware helper.** A helper (e.g. `neighbourSynergyGainByOwner(...)` returning `{ own, opponent }`) attributes each neighbour's marginal synergy to the acting seat or to another seat using `getSlotOwnerId(state, i)`; no owner filter is applied in single-player (N=1).
- **Community-space competitive value.** In competitive mode `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement(...)` credits only the acting player's neighbour synergy and subtracts the synergy anchored for other seats; `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gates community spaces on the ownership-aware net score.
- **Ordinary competitive placements.** `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` subtract the anchored opponent synergy from the placement score while leaving own income/synergy unchanged; income-producing businesses remain always eligible.
- **Single-player unchanged.** `scoreAction`, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` and `GreedyStrategy` produce identical results with no `ownerTaggedGrid`; `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` baselines hold.
- **Determinism preserved.** No RNG introduced; same seed + `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy` yields an identical action sequence.
- **Tests pass.** The tests from the sibling test item pass.
- **Doc-comments updated.** `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` / competitive-score comments document the `own − opponent` rule.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `neighbourSynergyGainByOwner(grid, placed, slotIndex, bonusPerNeighbor, owners)` reusing `computeSynergyBonus`.
2. Use it in `communitySpacePlacementValueAt` when `isCompetitiveMode(state)` — `neighbourIncome = own − opponent` — with an N=1 fallback to `neighbourSynergyGain`.
3. Apply the opponent-benefit term in `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore`.
4. Keep `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gating community spaces on the resulting `score > 0`.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sibling test item (test-first).

## Deliverables

- Ownership-aware placement scoring in `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts`

# Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge cards)

## Problem statement

Business and community-space cards are currently rendered with a neutral dark-grey
face (`#2f2f2f`); only a faint synergy-accent header bar, the 64×64 art backing and
the synergy icons carry the synergy colour. Players therefore cannot read a card's
synergy type — or, for a bridge card, both of its synergy types — directly from the
card face, which weakens at-a-glance planning when the market row mixes single- and
multi-synergy cards. The card face should be coloured by synergy type, and bridge
cards (exactly two synergy types) should show both colours, split top and bottom.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — scanning the market row and their street,
  wants to identify a card's synergy type(s) instantly without reading the icon row or
  opening a tooltip.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player scanning the market, I want each business/community-space
  card coloured by its synergy type, so that I can tell Food from Culture at a glance.
- As a Main Street player evaluating a bridge card, I want to see both of its synergy
  colours (top and bottom), so that I immediately understand it connects two clusters.
- As a player with colour-vision deficiency, I still want an unambiguous cue (the
  synergy icons), so that colour is not the only signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single-synergy face colour.** Every business and community-space card with
  exactly one synergy type renders its card face in that synergy type's face colour
  from a single shared, documented palette, replacing the current neutral `#2f2f2f`
  face. The mapping is the single source of truth used by every generator.
- **AC2 — Two-tone bridge face.** Every card with exactly two synergy types renders
  its face split horizontally into two colour bands — **top band = first entry in
  `synergyTypes`, bottom band = second entry** — using the same palette. The rounded
  card corners and the existing inner gradient / header-bar treatments are preserved,
  and neither band bleeds outside the rounded rectangle.
- **AC3 — Both synergies identifiable; colour is not the only cue.** Each bridge card
  continues to render **both** synergy icons (bottom-left), and the title/stat text
  remains white and legible on both bands; cards remain identifiable under hand
  overlap (~20 px) and street stacking (~23 px) (existing layout contract
  CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN). Cards with zero synergy types (event / upgrade / staff) keep
  their existing family colours unchanged.
- **AC4 — All render paths agree.** The static Node generator
  (`generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`), the runtime CSV fallback
  (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`) and the dynamic state-aware generator
  (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) all produce the same synergy colouring/split, and the
  pre-baked SVGs in `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` plus
  `csv-checksum.json` are regenerated.
- **AC5 — Tests.** Unit tests cover: single-synergy cards use the matching palette
  colour; bridge cards emit two bands with the correct top/bottom palette colours and
  band geometry; zero-synergy cards are unchanged; the TS and mjs generators agree;
  and the shipped static SVGs reflect the colouring (regression guard). Existing SVG
  tests (`card-svg-generator.test.ts`, `mjs-svg-generator.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`,
  currency/ongoing-cost tests) continue to pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, `README.md` where relevant, and the Main Street docs
  (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` bridge section and any card-rendering/design
  notes).
- **AC7 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Rendering-only:** no engine, rules, scoring, adjacency, balance, or card-data (CSV)
  changes. `synergyTypes` is already the source of truth.
- **One palette:** a single documented synergy→face-colour map is the source of truth.
  The `.mjs` static generator cannot import the TS module, so the values are duplicated
  in the two places with a test asserting agreement — following the existing pattern
  used for staff cost text.
- **Two types maximum today** (CSV distribution: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge,
  135 none). Behaviour for >2 synergy types is out of scope; the implementation must
  degrade safely (e.g. fall back to a single/first colour) rather than throw.
- **Preserve the existing card layout:** 64×64 left-art zone, text positions, cost
  badge, level badge, synergy icons and embedded art (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN).
- **UK English** in code comments and documentation.

## Existing state

- Runtime cards are rasterised from static SVGs generated by
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` (`generateCardSvg`) and refreshed
  from the CSV at runtime by `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts`), driven by `MainStreetSvgTextureManager`.
- `familyColor()` (mjs) and `cardColorScheme()` (TS) give business and community-space
  cards a neutral face (`#2f2f2f`); synergy colour is applied only to the graphic
  backing (`opacity 0.42`), the 20 px header bar (`opacity 0.18`) and the synergy icons.
- `synergyColor` (bright palette) is used for icons/accents; `CARD_BG` (dark palette)
  exists in the TS generator for `generateBusinessCardSvg` and is currently the only
  place a synergy-coloured face is used.
- 39 business/community-space cards: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge — Cafe, Food Truck,
  Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga Studio, Physiotherapist,
  Teahouse, Public Art.
- `generateBusinessCardSvg` (dynamic) is used only by tests today; the runtime texture
  path is the CSV/static pair — but it must stay consistent.

## Desired change

- Introduce a documented synergy→face-colour palette (reuse `CARD_BG`) and a helper
  that computes the face background: one colour for single-synergy cards, a top/bottom
  colour pair for bridge cards.
- Update the `.mjs` and TS generators to paint the face with that helper, splitting
  bridge faces horizontally (top = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom = `synergyTypes[1]`)
  inside the rounded rect (clip path or two rounded/clipped rects).
- Regenerate the static SVGs and `csv-checksum.json`.
- Add/update tests and documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — face background via palette +
  top/bottom split for bridge cards; expose the mapping for tests.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `cardColorScheme` /
  `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` and `generateBusinessCardSvg` face colouring + split;
  shared `CARD_BG` palette.
- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — canonical `synergyColor` (bright palette) reference;
  add the dark face palette here if it should be shared.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — regenerated, especially
  `biz-cafe.svg`, `biz-food-truck.svg`, `biz-gallery.svg`, `biz-spa.svg`,
  `biz-florist.svg`, `biz-juice-bar.svg`, `biz-yoga-studio.svg`, `biz-physio.svg`,
  `biz-teahouse.svg`, `cs-public-art.svg`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated checksum.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — read-only; verify the runtime CSV
  fallback picks up the colouring (no change expected).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — face-colour + bridge split
  assertions.
- `tests/main-street/mjs-svg-generator.test.ts` — static-SVG regression guard for the
  split + TS/mjs agreement.
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — verify no regression in art embedding with the
  new backgrounds.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — document the colour scheme / bridge two-tone rule.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN` (completed) — Synergy tooltip.
- `MS-0MTSAWSME004BH6S` (completed) — Add images for all cards.
- `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` (completed) — Competitive rendering: owner-coloured street,
  shared-market phase alternation, SFX.
- `MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327` (completed) — Move level label to left (same SVG layout code).
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` (open) — Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card
  (touches the art backing in the same generator).
- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` (open) — Identify different AI players (shared
  colour-blind-friendliness concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (palette):** use the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette for the card face
  (readable with white text), keeping the bright `synergyColor` palette for
  icons/accents. The producer may prefer the bright palette — a small, localised switch.
- **Assumption (split):** horizontal split, top band = first entry in the CSV
  `synergyTypes` order, bottom = second, matching the operator's "top and bottom".
- **Assumption (scope):** applies to business + community-space cards in all three
  generators; event/upgrade/staff keep family colours; no >2-synergy cards exist today.
- **Risk (generator drift):** the mjs and TS generators hold separate copies of the
  colour logic. Mitigation: shared constant values plus an agreement test.
- **Risk (contrast/readability):** full colour faces may reduce text contrast,
  especially under the 0.18 header overlay. Mitigation: dark palette, keep the synergy
  icons as a secondary cue, and visually check in the browser test.
- **Risk (stale static assets):** forgetting to regenerate the static SVGs / checksum
  leaves the game showing old faces. Mitigation: regenerate in the same change and add
  a shipped-SVG regression test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** card-art redesign, per-owner tile tints, or synergy-icon
  additions are out of scope — record as linked work items, do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive round was run — the operator's seed directive plus repo research
sufficed to draft a clear brief. The design defaults below are recorded as **assumed
(recommended option)**; the producer may override any of them before implementation.

- **Q1 (palette):** "Which palette should colour the card face?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette (Food `#5D4037`,
  Culture `#1565C0`, Commerce `#2E7D32`, Service `#6A1B9A`, Entertainment `#C62828`,
  Health `#00838F`), because white card text stays legible; the bright `synergyColor`
  palette stays for icons/accents. Source: repo research of
  `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.CARD_BG` and `MainStreetCardsUtils.synergyColor`.
  Status: **assumed**.
- **Q2 (split):** "How are a bridge card's two colours arranged?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): horizontal split, top band = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom band =
  `synergyTypes[1]`, matching the operator's wording "two colours top and bottom".
  Source: operator directive. Status: **assumed**.
- **Q3 (scope / render paths):** "Which cards and which generators?" — Answer (agent

# Spread reputation pedestrians evenly around the street edges

## Problem statement

The reputation pedestrians (the on-street crowd that visually represents the
player's reputation) all enter the street from the four block corners and then
each walks to the **nearest** occupied business. Because the spawn points are
concentrated at the corners, the crowd clusters into whichever businesses sit
nearest those corners instead of being spread fairly evenly around the street,
so the visual representation of reputation looks lopsided.

## Users

- **Player (reputation visualisation):** sees the crowd as a stand-in for their
  reputation score; a lopsided crowd misrepresents the state and looks broken.
  - *As a player, I want the reputation crowd spread around the street so my
    reputation reads as a distributed, healthy population rather than a clot in
    one shop.*
- **Producer (manual audit):** rejected the corner-clustered distribution and
  wants figures to enter spread out around the four edges.
  - *As the producer, I want figures to enter spread out around the street so
    that when they head to the nearest business the crowd is naturally evenly
    distributed.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Perimeter spawn distribution.** New figures spawn at points distributed
   along all four edges of the road-network perimeter — including mid-edge
   positions — rather than only at the four block-corner nodes. A pure/behaviour
   test asserts that across a seeded run of `spawnPedestrianFigure` calls the
   spawn origins cover all four edges and that at least some figures originate
   away from corner nodes.
2. **Relatively even spread.** The spawn distribution is *relatively even*
   around the perimeter: over a seeded run the per-edge spawn counts fall within
   a defined tolerance of an equal share (roughly `N/4` per edge), and/or the
   perimeter positions are stratified so no region dominates. Deterministic with
   the presentation PRNG; a test asserts the per-edge balance.
3. **Road/lane invariants preserved.** Spawned figures still start on a road
   **lane** (offset from the centre-line, on a road band) and heading along a
   valid road segment (`from`/`target` endpoints of the perimeter segment).
   Existing lane/on-road assertions continue to pass.
4. **Nearest-business seeking unchanged.** Walking figures still head for the
   nearest occupied cell (MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2) and still walk deliberately into
   it with no teleporting; a behaviour test asserts that an evenly spread crowd
   entering shops distributes across more than one occupied business (rather
   than clustering in a single nearest shop).
5. **All spawn paths affected.** The even perimeter distribution applies to
   every spawn path — initial creation, `startNewTurn()` respawn, and live
   population reconciliation (`setPopulation` gains mid-turn) — not just the
   turn-start path. A test asserts reconciled/gained figures also spawn on the
   spread perimeter.
6. **Presentation-only behaviour preserved.** Reduced Motion and replay/headless
   exemptions are unchanged; no gameplay RNG is consumed; presentation-only
   failures are still swallowed; the credited reputation totals are unchanged.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` is updated to
   describe the even, edge-distributed spawn (replacing the "enter from a block
   corner / four corners" description), including unit test coverage for the
   distribution.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only layer: must never mutate game state, the transcript, or
  the turn flow; every public method stays defensive.
- Must use the module-local seeded presentation PRNG (`createPresentationRng`)
  and never the seeded gameplay RNG or `Math.random`.
- Must not change the figure count rule (`floor(reputation / 50)`) or the
  reputation-phase sourcing/25%-shopping guarantee.
- Keep the change surgical: no unrelated refactoring of the pedestrian layer.

## Existing state

- `spawnPedestrianFigure` (`src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts`) picks a random
  entry from `network.corners` and a random adjacent neighbour, then places the
  figure on the lane at that corner. All figures therefore originate at the four
  corners.
- `stepPedestrianFigure` re-resolves `nearestShop(figure, shops)` every frame
  and steers the figure toward the nearest occupied cell; if all figures start
  near the corners this concentrates them in the corner-nearest businesses.
- Docs (`docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`) currently state figures "always
  enter from a block corner" and "wander onto the street from the four corners
  of the block (`network.corners`)".
- Prior related work: `MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ` (road-walking / shop entry),
  `MS-0MUZ6CGSV002WTYM` (lanes, deliberate entry, persistence),
  `MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2` (nearest occupied cell seeking),
  `MS-0MUZ9CKT60094CXO` (in-shop spread).

## Desired change

Distribute spawn points (and thus entry points) evenly around the four edges of
the block perimeter rather than at the corner nodes only. Figures continue to
walk the road lanes and continue to seek the nearest occupied business, so an
evenly spread entry distribution yields an evenly spread crowd in the shops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — `spawnPedestrianFigure` and a new
  perimeter-distribution helper (stratified perimeter spawn points); keep
  `nearestShop` seeking intact.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — any new spawn-distribution constants.
- `src/MainStreetMapView.ts` — road-band/perimeter geometry helpers if needed.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — update the spawn/entry description.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-layer.test.ts` — spawn distribution tests.

## Risks

- **Distribution still imperfect when businesses are sparse.** If few cells are
  occupied, an even entry spread can still funnel several figures into the same
  nearest shop. Mitigation: scope is entry distribution only; shop seeking stays
  nearest-cell by design (producer phrasing).
- **Mid-turn spawns perturb the balance.** Live gains added between turns could
  bias one edge. Mitigation: apply the same stratified distribution on every
  spawn path; test reconciliation spawns.
- **Pure-helper coupling.** Changing spawn geometry could break existing
  lane/on-road invariants. Mitigation: keep the lane placement helper and assert
  the existing on-road/lane distance in the new tests.
- **Scope creep.** Related opportunities (retuning crowd density, per-seat
  competitive crowds, business-aware even assignment) are **out of scope** and
  should be raised as separate discovered-from work items, not absorbed here.

## Related work

See "Related work (automated report)" on the work item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** – Visual representation of reputation (parent epic)
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** – Competitive state model: per-player resources, owner-tagged street (completed)
- **MS-0MUVBH589001L7NL** – Competitive game ends on AI seat failure — reputation collapse or bankruptcy (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: around, block, business, corners, crowd (+12 more)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: around, block, business, cluster, edges (+11 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: block, business, corners, edges, enter (+10 more)


## Assumptions

- "Four edges" = the four sides of the road-network perimeter (the block
  boundary); the "street" is the road grid the figures already walk.
- "Relatively even" is enforced deterministically via a stratified/balanced
  distribution rather than left to chance, so it is testable.
- Shop targeting stays *nearest occupied cell* (per the producer's phrasing
  "when they go to the nearest business"); only the entry distribution changes.
- The even distribution applies to every spawn path, including mid-turn
  population gains.
- Buildings/roads/geometry are unchanged; this is a distribution change only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Interview skipped** — the seed intent from the producer was sufficiently
specific to draft this brief without an interview round (intake §1: skip the
interview when the seed context suffices). The points below are the
assumptions made while drafting; each is a candidate question the producer may
correct at review time.

- Q: Does "spread out around the street" mean spawning only at corners but
  with varied offsets, or distributing entry points along the full four edges?
  — Answer (derived from producer seed intent): distribute along the full four
  edges, including mid-edge positions, not only the corners. Source:
  interactive producer message: "Rather than have them all enter at the corners
  have them enter spread out around the street … relatively even around the 4
  edges".
- Q: Should shop targeting change to an explicit round-robin/even assignment
  across occupied businesses? — Answer (derived): no; keep *nearest occupied
  cell* seeking, relying on the even entry distribution to spread the crowd
  naturally. Source: producer phrasing "so that they will naturally be evenly
  spread when they go to the nearest business".
- Q: Does the even distribution apply to mid-turn population gains as well as
  turn-start? — Answer (assumption): yes, all spawn paths. Source: producer
  intent that figures "enter spread out around the street" generally.
- Q: What tolerance defines "relatively even"? — Answer (assumption): enforced
  deterministically via balanced/stratified perimeter placement, verified by a
  per-edge balance test rather than a statistical threshold. Source: agent
  drafting decision; OPEN QUESTION for the producer if a different tolerance is
  expected.
- Priority: explicitly set to `medium` by the operator (`--priority medium`),
  which takes precedence over classification.

# Intake Brief: Divide the competitive score target by the number of players

**Work item:** MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE · `feature` · `critical`
**Seed intent (operator):** "The target score for a game should be divided by the number of players."
**Supersedes:** MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D (Competitive mode: halve the score target per AI opponent) — producer decision 2026-10-08, Q1 = (a).

## Headline

In competitive (human vs AI) games the win target is currently the full single-player
`config.winThreshold` (Easy 10000 / Medium 12000 / Hard 15000), so a game against more
opponents does not get any shorter per seat. This item makes the effective target the base
threshold **divided by the number of players** (`playerCount`, human + AI) and **rounded to
the nearest 50**, and makes every engine and player-facing use of the target agree on that one
derived value.

## Problem statement

Competitive mode uses a single shared `config.winThreshold` for the first-to-threshold win
check, the AI look-ahead and every player-facing score readout. The operator wants the target
score to scale down with the number of players so a larger roster still reaches the win
condition in a comparable run length. Today no such scaling exists anywhere.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the "x / y" target shown in the HUD, score tooltip and help panel to match
  the value the engine actually awards a win at, and to be achievable in a sensible number of
  turns regardless of how many AI seats are in the game.
- **Balance designer / producer** — wants one authoritative, testable formula for the
  competitive target so future balancing levers are unambiguous.
- **Developer** — wants a single source of truth (helper) rather than the same arithmetic
  duplicated across engine, AI and UI.

User story: *As a player starting a competitive game against two AI opponents, I want the score
target divided by the number of players so the race stays winnable in a comparable run length
to single-player.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Effective target formula.** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`.
- **AC2 — Consistent everywhere.** The HUD `Score: x / y` line, the score tooltip (`x / y`, "remaining to win") and the help panel "Reach N points to win" text all show the effective competitive threshold, never the base value.
- **AC3 — Single-player unchanged.** Single-player (no `players[]` / `playerCount` undefined) continues to use the base `winThreshold`, which is already a multiple of 50 so the rounding is a no-op.
- **AC4 — AI parity.** The AI look-ahead `aiPlanningHorizon` and the per-seat `aiCompetitivePlanningHorizon` use the effective win threshold, so the AI plans toward the win condition it is racing toward.
- **AC5 — Save/load round-trip.** A resumed competitive game re-derives the effective win threshold from the persisted `playerCount`; no stale threshold survives a load.
- **AC6 — Testing and validation.** New Vitest coverage for AC1–AC5 (engine, AI, UI strings, serialisation) and the full project test suite passes; the new tests fail against the pre-change code.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** The competitive win-condition description in `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` states the `base / playerCount`, rounded to the nearest 50, effective win threshold rule, and touched code comments are updated.

*Metric:* each AC is pass/fail via the tests named in its child slices — see the plan decomposition.
## Constraints

- **Single-player must not change.** Division by one player is the only single-player effect;
  no behaviour shift there.
- **Do not change base difficulty presets** (Easy/Medium/Hard `winThreshold` values in
  `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`) — derive the effective value at consumption time.
- **Do not change** challenge-complete instant win, bankruptcy, reputation-collapse,
  last-standing, or endless-mode continuation semantics (MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4).
- **One source of truth.** Introduce a single pure helper for the effective threshold and use it
  at every engine/AI/UI site; do not duplicate the arithmetic.
- **UK English** in all comments, docs and UI copy.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `config.winThreshold` is a single shared value (Easy 10000, Medium 12000, Hard 15000) in
  `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`.
- Competitive win check compares each `PlayerRecord.score` to `config.winThreshold`
  (`checkCompetitiveEndConditions`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:1058`), including the
  endless-mode branch (`endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'`).
- AI look-ahead reads `config.winThreshold` directly
  (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:134` in `aiPlanningHorizon`, and `:1821` in
  `aiCompetitivePlanningHorizon`).
- Player-facing displays read `config.winThreshold`:
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts:221` (HUD `Score: x / y`),
  `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:290` (score tooltip),
  `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts:128` (help "Reach N points to win", fed from
  `buildMainStreetHelpContent(s.state.config)` in `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts:365`).
- `playerCount` is set by `createCompetitiveState` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:586`) and is
  already serialised/restored (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts:93`, `:649`).
- Competitive rosters are bounded: `MIN_AI_OPPONENTS = 1`, `MAX_AI_OPPONENTS = 3`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameSelection.ts:32-33`), so `P ∈ {2, 3, 4}`.
- No `effectiveWinThreshold` / effective-target helper exists today (grep confirmed).

## Desired change

Add a pure helper in `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` (re-exported via `src/MainStreetState.ts`
if needed):

```ts
/**
 * Effective win threshold. Competitive games divide the difficulty base
 * threshold by the number of seats (human + AI), rounded to the nearest 50
 * so the target stays a round, displayable number. Single-player has no
 * `playerCount`, so it resolves to the base threshold unchanged.
 */
export function effectiveWinThreshold(state: MainStreetState): number {
  const players = state.playerCount ?? 1;
  return Math.round(state.config.winThreshold / players / 50) * 50;
}
```

Route every win-check, AI-horizon and player-facing display site through it. Single-player
resolves to the base value because `playerCount` is undefined. Because `playerCount` is already
persisted, save/load needs no new field — only a test asserting the re-derived value.

Worked values (base → effective):

| Base (preset) | P=2 | P=3 | P=4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Easy 10000 | 5000 | 3350 | 2500 |
| Medium 12000 | 6000 | 4000 | 3000 |
| Hard 15000 | 7500 | 5000 | 3750 |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — home for the new pure `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` helper
  (alongside `computeScore`), re-exported via `src/MainStreetState.ts` if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — use the helper in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
  (single-player path stays `checkEndConditions`), including the endless-mode branch.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `aiPlanningHorizon` and `aiCompetitivePlanningHorizon` use the
  helper instead of `config.winThreshold`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — HUD `Score: x / y` denominator.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildScoreTooltip` threshold/remaining lines.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help panel "Reach N points to win" receives the effective
  threshold from state; caller `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` passes it.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — read-only reference; `playerCount` already persisted.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — read-only reference; base presets must not change.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-ai-win.test.ts` — extend the competitive win-check
  coverage for P = 2..4.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — extend the AI horizon coverage.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-hud.test.ts` — HUD `Score: x / y` string.
- `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts` — score tooltip `x / y` and "remaining to win".
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — help "Reach N points to win" string.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-save-load.test.ts` — re-derived threshold after load.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Section 7 win-condition rule.

## Plan decomposition

Four test-first vertical slices (each writes failing tests first, then implementation, then a
green suite):

1. **Effective threshold helper and competitive win check** — MS-0MUZK64F8000XYO0 *(high;
   prerequisite for 2–4)* — the pure helper, the standard and endless competitive win check,
   single-player parity, and the save/load regression guards. *(AC1, AC3, AC5)*
2. **AI look-ahead uses the effective win threshold** — MS-0MUZK64R5008Z8MA *(depends on 1)* —
   both planning-horizon helpers. *(AC4)*
3. **Player-facing win target consistency HUD tooltip help** — MS-0MUZK652V001L71C *(depends on
   1)* — HUD, score tooltip and help panel. *(AC2)*
4. **Document the competitive target rule and validate the suite** — MS-0MUZK65EI004X4UB
   *(depends on 1)* — the Section 7 docs rule and the documented-value sweep. *(AC7)*

AC6 (new tests fail pre-change; full `npm test` green) is verified inside every slice. The
persistence assertions in slice 1 are regression guards (they are green once the helper lands,
but fail if the `?? 1` default is removed or a derived threshold is persisted).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D** — Competitive mode: halve the score target per AI opponent.
  **Superseded by this item** (producer decision 2026-10-08, Q1 = a). Its `base × 0.5^N`
  formula agrees with `base / P` only at two players; it is closed, not implemented.
- **MS-0MUXLGCQC000W7ZE** — Add test cases for AI and human win threshold in competitive mode
  (open) — test precedent for competitive threshold behaviour.
- **MS-0MUXLP6V00075IQY** — Fix win/loss attribution in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
  (blocked) — touches the same function; slice 1 should be rebased on it if it lands first.
- **MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV** — Confirm win thresholds / run length as the difficulty lever (open) —
  balance context for run length.
- **MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30** — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
  (completed) — origin of the shared first-to-threshold rule.
- **MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4** — Competitive endless continuation beyond win threshold (completed) —
  endless-mode branch must use the effective threshold without changing semantics.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4** – Competitive endless continuation (beyond win threshold) (completed)
- **MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0** – Per-seat animated competitive closing (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** – Game-mode selector UI (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: competitive, discovered, game, intent, mode, number, operator, players, score, seed, should, target
- `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` — matched: competitive, game, intent, mode, number, operator, opponent, players, score, seed, should, target
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: game, intent, mode, number, operator, opponent, players, score, seed, should, target

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE.md`.

## Assumptions

- **"Number of players" = total seats, including the human** (i.e. `state.playerCount`), not
  "number of AI opponents". Confirmed by the producer decision on Q1 (2026-10-08).
- **Rounding:** the quotient is rounded to the **nearest 50** (`Math.round(base / P / 50) * 50`),
  so Easy/P=3 → 3350 rather than 3333. Ties round up (`Math.round` semantics). Confirmed by the
  producer decision on Q2 (2026-10-08).
- **Competitive-only effect:** single-player has one player, so division by one leaves the base
  value unchanged by construction.
- The operator's `base / P` formula is the current intent and **supersedes** the compounding
  `0.5^N` formula recorded on MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D; that item is closed as superseded.

## Risks

- **Engine/UI divergence** — if any display site keeps reading `config.winThreshold` the player
  sees a target the engine does not use. *Mitigation:* single helper + a grep/test sweep for
  remaining win-threshold decision sites (exclude single-player/legacy paths deliberately).
- **Legacy saves** missing `playerCount` must default to divisor 1, not break. *Mitigation:*
  `?? 1` default plus a load test.
- **Balance drift** — a lower target shortens competitive runs, possibly interacting with the
  run-length lever. *Mitigation:* flag to MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV; keep the change a single derived
  formula so it is trivially reversible.
- **Scope creep** into single-player or difficulty presets. *Mitigation:* Constraints above;
  log any follow-on as separate work.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q0 (seed intent).** What is the requested behaviour? — **Answer (operator):** "The target
  score for a game should be divided by the number of players." Source: `/intake` invocation,
  2026-10-08. Priority `critical` supplied by the operator.
- **Q1 (duplicate / formula conflict).** Does this item supersede the producer-confirmed formula
  on MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D (`base × 0.5^N`, N = AI opponents), or should both be reconciled?
  Options were: (a) adopt `base / P` and supersede MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D; (b) adopt `base × 0.5^N`
  and rewrite this item; (c) defer and reconcile later. — **Answer (operator, 2026-10-08):** (a).
  Agent recommendation was (a). MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D is recorded as superseded by
  MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE and closed. Evidence: this work item's plan session, 2026-10-08.
- **Q2 (rounding).** For non-integer quotients (e.g. Easy 10000 ÷ 3), how should the effective
  target round? Options were: `Math.round` → 3333; `Math.ceil` → 3334; `Math.floor` → 3333. —
  **Answer (operator, 2026-10-08):** "round to the nearest 50", i.e. 3333 → **3350**. Final:
  `Math.round(base / P / 50) * 50` with ties rounding up. Agent recommendation had been
  `Math.round` (nearest integer); the operator chose the stronger nearest-50 rule, which
  supersedes that recommendation. Evidence: this work item's plan session, 2026-10-08.

**Open questions: none.** Both intake questions are resolved.

# Restructure the documentation: separate development docs from gameplay docs

**Discovered from:** `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C` (rendering the storyline graph surfaced
that `docs/main-street/` mixes audience-facing gameplay documentation with
engineering/process documentation).

## Problem statement

`docs/main-street/` is a single flat directory that mixes two very different
audiences and lifecycles:

- **Gameplay / player-facing reference** — `storylines.md`,
  `content-design-and-progression.md`, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `card-catalog.md`, `card-dimensions.md`, `specialization-skills.md`,
  `ux-visual-audio.md`, `tutorial-localization.md`, `playtest-scenarios.md`,
  `the-build-gdd.md`.
- **Development / engineering & evidence** — `balancing-methodology.md`,
  `balance-analysis-api.md`, `balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`,
  `further-balancing-recommendations.md`, `monte-carlo-*`, `*evidence.md`,
  `prd-*.md`, `ai-strategy.md`, `analysis/`, `screenshots/`, generated
  artefacts (`storyline-graph.mmd`, `storyline-manifest.json`,
  `expanded-card-manifest.json`, `card-catalog-baseline.json`).

A reader looking for gameplay rules has to wade through balance experiments,
PRDs and evidence bundles; an engineer looking for process docs has to filter
out player-facing prose. Links between the two trees are also fragile
(relative paths, `example-games/` staleness — see `MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5`).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the documentation split by audience — gameplay docs
separate from development docs — with stable, cross-linked structure, so each
audience can find what it needs and the docs build/guards stay green.

## Proposed shape (to be confirmed in intake/plan)

- `docs/game/` (or `docs/players/`) — gameplay-rule and content reference.
- `docs/dev/` — engineering, balance methodology, PRDs, evidence, process.
- Generated artefacts under a single `assets/` (or `generated/`) location.
- Cross-links updated; doc-drift guards and path-based tests updated.

## Acceptance Criteria (provisional — to be finalised by intake/plan)

1. **Audience split** — gameplay docs and development docs live in separate,
   documented trees; the split is stated in a top-level docs index.

# Slice 1: Effective-threshold helper and competitive win check

**Parent:** MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE (Competitive mode: divide the score target by the number of players) · slice 1 of 4
**Test-first:** write the failing Vitest cases below **before** adding the helper.

## Goal

Introduce the single source of truth for the competitive win target and make the competitive
win check use it, so a game with `P` seats (human + AI) is won at
`Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50`.

Worked values (base → effective): Easy 10000 → P=2 5000, P=3 3350, P=4 2500;
Medium 12000 → 6000 / 4000 / 3000; Hard 15000 → 7500 / 5000 / 3750.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. Slice tests pin Easy P=2 5000, P=3 3350, P=4 2500 and are written red before the helper exists.
- **AC2 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. A single pure `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` returns `Math.round(state.config.winThreshold / (state.playerCount ?? 1) / 50) * 50`, and no other site in `src/` duplicates the division.
- **AC3 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. The competitive win check compares each per-owner score against the effective win threshold for P = 2, 3, 4 and declares that seat `competitiveWinnerId` with `endReason = 'score_threshold'`.
- **AC4 (parent AC3).** Single-player (no `players[]` / `playerCount` undefined) continues to use the base `winThreshold`, which is already a multiple of 50 so the rounding is a no-op. The competitive entry point delegates to `checkEndConditions` and an explicit assertion pins the unchanged base value.
- **AC5 (parent AC5).** A resumed competitive game re-derives the effective win threshold from the persisted `playerCount`; no stale threshold survives a load. A serialise then deserialise round-trip of a P=3 Easy state re-derives 3350; a legacy save with no `playerCount` yields the base threshold.
- **AC6 (parent AC6).** New Vitest coverage for AC1–AC5 (engine, AI, UI strings, serialisation) and the full project test suite passes; the new tests fail against the pre-change code. (this slice: helper, competitive win check, persistence guards).
- **AC7.** The endless-mode branch uses the effective win threshold and keeps `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and its idempotent re-entry behaviour unchanged.

*Metric:* unit tests for AC1–AC4 red then green; source grep for AC2; regression-guard test for AC5; `npm test` for AC6 and AC7.
## Minimal implementation

- Add `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` to `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` with a doc comment
  stating the competitive `base / playerCount`, nearest-50 rule and the single-player no-op.
- Re-export it from `src/MainStreetState.ts` if consumers import through the barrel.
- Replace `state.config.winThreshold` with the helper in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
  (both the standard and endless branches) in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`; leave
  `checkEndConditions` untouched.
- Add the round-trip and legacy-save guards to the competitive save/load suite.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`
- `src/MainStreetState.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-ai-win.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-save-load.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None. This slice is the prerequisite for slices 2–4.
- Note: MS-0MUXLP6V00075IQY (Fix win/loss attribution in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`,
  blocked) touches the same function — rebase on it if it lands first.

## Deliverables

- `effectiveWinThreshold` helper with unit coverage.
- Competitive win check (standard + endless) routed through the helper.
- Persistence regression guards.

# Ask about the tutorial before the single-player/competitive choice

## Problem statement

At scene boot the blocking "New Game" overlay asks the player to choose
Single-player vs Competitive **before** the tutorial offer is shown. A player
who actually wants the guided tutorial must therefore pick a game mode first,
even though the tutorial can only ever be played single-player — so the mode
choice is either wasted or misleading. The tutorial decision should be asked
first, and choosing the tutorial should commit the player to single-player
without an unnecessary mode choice.

## Users

- **First-time player (tutorial wanters).** "As a first-time player, I want to
  be asked whether I want the tutorial *before* I am asked to pick a mode, so
  that I am not forced to make a mode choice that the tutorial will ignore."
- **First-time player (tutorial decliners).** "As a first-time player who
  skips the tutorial, I want the Single-player/Competitive selector to appear
  immediately so I can start the game I actually want."
- **Returning player.** "As a returning player (tutorial already completed or
  skipped), I want the mode selector to appear straight away, unchanged from
  today."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On boot, when the tutorial offer is eligible, the tutorial offer modal is
   presented **before** the New Game mode selector (Single-player vs
   Competitive); the mode selector is not visible while the tutorial offer is
   waiting.
2. Selecting **Start Tutorial** starts the existing scripted tutorial as a
   single-player game and the New Game mode selector is not shown for that
   boot. (The tutorial is only available in single-player.)
3. Selecting **Skip for now** on the tutorial offer presents the New Game
   mode selector next, and confirming it starts the selected mode exactly as
   today.
4. When the tutorial offer is **not** eligible (completed, already skipped,
   replay mode, or disabled), the New Game mode selector is presented as the
   first boot modal, exactly as today.
5. The deferred week banner still fires **exactly once** and only after the
   player has committed to playing (after mode confirmation, or suppressed
   for the tutorial path as today). It must not fire while any boot modal is
   waiting for a choice.
6. A browser smoke test asserts the modal ordering: tutorial offer visible
   first; after skipping, the mode selector is visible.
7. A unit test asserts the ordering decision in
   `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` (tutorial offer before mode selector,
   and the mode selector is skipped entirely when the tutorial is started).
8. The scene-restart / menu round-trip behaviour is preserved: the boot flow
   is presented once per boot, and re-presented after `scene.restart()` /
   `scene.start()` (regression guard).
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (for example
   the onboarding flow section of `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md`).
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No changes to the tutorial script/steps, tutorial content, or competitive
  gameplay/state semantics.
- Reuse the existing `TutorialOfferModal` and `MainStreetNewGameOverlay`
  components and the existing localisation keys; no new user-facing strings
  are required unless the producer asks for an explicit "tutorial is
  single-player" note (see Assumptions).
- Must not regress the deferred-banner timing guarantees currently pinned by
  `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts`.
- Must not regress the once-per-boot selector guard
  (`newGameSelectionMade` / `resetNewGameSelectionFlag`).

## Existing state

- `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerTutorial.ts` currently shows
  `newGameOverlay` first and only calls `showTutorialOfferOnly` from the
  overlay's `onConfirm` callback.
- `TutorialOfferModal.onSkip` (wired in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) currently calls
  `s.playDeferredWeekBanner()` directly.
- `TutorialOfferModal.onStartTutorial` already builds a single-player
  tutorial state via `createTutorialScenario()` and starts the tutorial flow.
- `applyNewGameSelection` (in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`) rebuilds state only for
  competitive; single-player keeps the existing state.
- Eligibility is decided by `shouldShowTutorialOffer` in
  `src/TutorialState.ts` (`not_seen` shows; `completed`/`skipped` do not;
  `forceShowOffer` overrides; `replayMode`/`disableTutorial` suppress).
- The current implementation order contradicts the onboarding flow documented
  in `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` §5 (tutorial check before normal
  run), which predates the competitive mode selector.

## Desired change

Reorder the boot flow so the tutorial offer is the **first** blocking modal:

1. If `showIfEligible` returns true → show the tutorial offer modal.
   - **Start Tutorial** → run the existing single-player tutorial; do not show
     the mode selector this boot.
   - **Skip for now** → show the New Game mode selector.
2. If the offer is ineligible → show the New Game mode selector.
3. After the mode selector is confirmed → `applyNewGameSelection` then play
   the deferred week banner (exactly once).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerTutorial.ts` — reorder
  `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` / `showTutorialOfferOnly` so the offer
  precedes the selector.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — rewire
  `onStartTutorial` / `onSkip` callbacks to the reordered flow; keep the
  tutorial single-player setup and the deferred-banner hand-off.
- `src/scenes/TutorialOfferModal.ts` — skip callback should no longer assume
  it owns the deferred-banner hand-off (if the reorder moves that
  responsibility).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameOverlay.ts` — only if the once-per-boot guard
  needs adjusting.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-new-game-restart.test.ts` — update ordering
  expectations for the selector guard.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-offer-modal.test.ts` — add ordering/decision
  coverage where testable without Phaser.
- `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts` — pin the deferred-banner
  timing under the new order.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` — update the onboarding flow section
  to state that the tutorial offer precedes the mode selector.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** — Game-mode selector UI (introduced the current
  boot-time selector ordering).
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — Playable AI competitive mode (parent epic of the
  selector).
- Automated related-work report appended by `/skill:find-related`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — no copy change.** The modal body/buttons keep their current
  localised copy. The "tutorial is single-player" fact is enforced by the flow
  (choosing the tutorial skips the mode selector) rather than stated in the
  UI. If the producer wants the modal copy to say "single-player", that is an
  additive copy/CSV change.
- **Assumption — tutorial start implies single-player.** "Start Tutorial"
  never shows the mode selector, matching the constraint that the tutorial is
  single-player only.
- **Risk — deferred-banner timing.** Moving the skip hand-off must preserve
  "fires exactly once, never while a modal is waiting". Covered by AC5/AC6.
- **Risk — guard interplay.** The `newGameSelectionMade` once-per-boot guard
  must not suppress the selector when the tutorial offer is skipped, and must
  not show the selector after the tutorial is started.
- **Risk — stale browser tests.** `tests/**/*.browser.test.ts` are excluded
  from `npm run test` (unit project only), so browser-ordering tests must be
  run explicitly via the browser profile to verify AC6.
- **Scope creep.** Repositioning/replay of the tutorial from Settings and any
  "tutorial is single-player" copy change are out of scope unless requested;
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the New Game mode selector be skipped entirely when the player
  chooses Start Tutorial (i.e. the tutorial always runs single-player)?" —
  Answer (operator, seed instruction): "If the player wants to play the
  tutorial they can only play single player. Ask if they want the tutorial
  before asking if they want to play single or competitive." Source:
  `/intake` seed command.
- Q: "Should the tutorial offer modal copy explicitly state that the tutorial
  is single-player only?" — Answer: OPEN QUESTION (not specified in the seed).
  Assumption recorded: no copy change; enforced by flow. Research: modal copy
  is localised in `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` and covered by
  `tests/main-street/tutorial-i18n.test.ts` / `tutorial-csv.test.ts`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ** – Reroll to cost more (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** – Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD (completed)
- **MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4** – Turns do not bank when playing against AI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac5, acceptance, actually, add, additive (+229 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, already, always (+176 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac6, acceptance, actually, add, additive (+172 more)

Verify the reordered flow end-to-end in a browser profile, including the
deferred-banner timing guarantees.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A browser smoke test asserts the modal ordering: tutorial offer visible first; after skipping, the mode selector is visible.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a browser test (e.g. `tests/main-street/tutorial-offer-ordering.browser.test.ts`) asserting offer-before-selector and selector-after-skip.
- Extend/pin `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts` for deferred-banner timing under the new order (fires exactly once; never while a modal is waiting).
- Run the browser test profile explicitly (browser tests are excluded from the unit project).

## Key Files (predicted)
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-offer-ordering.browser.test.ts` (new)
- `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts`

## Deliverables
- Browser ordering + banner-timing regression coverage.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Reorder tutorial-offer boot flow.
data.title: Browser modal-ordering and banner-timing tests

data.description:
## Goal

Track the residual below-target expensive-tier upgrades left after MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M.

## Context

discovered-from:MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M. On the canonical `mc-balance` Medium profile (200 seeds, 60 turns, greedy), the branching level-0 prerequisites `upg-drive-in` (cost 700) and `upg-wellness-center` (cost 900) remain at/near 0% M1 because they compete for the single upgrade market slot with the standard path (`upg-imax`, `upg-resort-spa`) weighted by MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W. Raising their `drawWeight` lifted them but nudged the level-2 capstone `upg-luxury-retreat` below 5%, so MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M left them unchanged rather than over-tune the market.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Canonical before/after Monte Carlo evidence (200 seeds, `mc-balance`, 60 turns, greedy Easy/Medium/Hard) records M1 for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`.
2. A card-data-only change (cost/`incomeBonus`/`drawWeight`) lifts both to >=5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones below 5% and without breaking the Easy >= Medium >= Hard win-rate ladder.
3. Full test suite passes.

## Constraints

Card data only; no engine-rule change. If unreachable, document the shortfall and escalate separately.
data.title: Residual expensive-tier branching upgrades below pick-rate target

data.description:
## Goal
As a Main Street player, I want installed entitled packs' cards dealt into my game and restored on load, so new content is persistent and save-compatible.

Cross-repo child of Tableau-Card-Engine CG-0MUZIS410002Z8EH (epic CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB, DLC support for card packs). The core contract/loader/merge landed in the engine (F1-F7); this item is the Main Street consumer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts resolves active packs through the core loader/client and feeds base CARD_DATA_RAW + pack rows through the core merge into a single loadTemplatesFromCsv entry point; pack cards deal and appear in play.
- Saves persist the active pack ids + versions + the merged checksum; load restores the same pool.
- A missing or disabled pack degrades gracefully: warn, continue with base content, and refuse only when a live card instance requires a missing template.
- No scattered ad-hoc merges: there is one documented merge entry point.
- Cross-repo changes are committed and pushed to the game repo's dev branch and recorded in the Main Street Worklog store.

## Minimal Implementation
- New src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts; extend MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts and MainStreetStateSerialize.ts; bump the ./core submodule to the engine commit carrying the card-pack merge/loader.

## Test Plan
- Unit (Main Street repo): base+pack merge, template accessors, save/load round-trip, missing-pack degradation.
data.title: Main Street pack merge & persistence

data.description:
## Goal
As a Main Street player, I want an SLL-positioned card-pack listing where I can see lock state and enable/disable packs, and packs must load before the game starts.

Cross-repo child of Tableau-Card-Engine CG-0MUZIS4KZ003R1HP (epic CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB, DLC support for card packs). Core listing/loader/merge landed in the engine (F1-F7); Main Street merge/persistence landed in F8 (MS-0MV07GNUU005E536).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The reusable core CardPackListing is wired into Main Street's overlay UI, positioned via SLL only.
- The listing reflects installed/unlocked/locked state; locked packs cannot be enabled; entitled packs can be toggled.
- Pack discovery completes before scene setup, with a safe base-content fallback if it fails.
- Toggling a pack refreshes the card pool consistently (refusing only when a live card would be stranded), and reduced-motion/mute behaviour is unchanged.
- Cross-repo changes are committed and pushed to the game repo's dev branch and recorded in the Main Street Worklog store.

## Minimal Implementation
- MainStreetOverlayContent.showCardPacksDialog + a Settings-area entry (HUD button), MainStreetCardPacks bootstrap/applyEnabled helpers, await pack discovery in createMainStreetGame.ts / main.ts and in the scene lifecycle.

## Test Plan
- Unit (Main Street repo): boot discovery + fallback, enabled-set preference round-trip, toggle re-merge/orphan refusal, listing input.
- Browser (Main Street repo): the listing opens, renders installed/locked rows, a locked pack cannot be enabled, and an entitled pack can be disabled.
data.title: Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring

data.description:
## Goal
As a Main Street player, I need confidence that an installed card pack flows through the whole pipeline — core renderer loader → deterministic CSV merge → Main Street template application → save → load — and that a missing pack degrades gracefully.

Cross-repo verification child of the core DLC epic CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB (core feature F10 CG-0MUZIS56500806DE).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A single integration test materialises a real fixture content directory (the committed Main Street reference pack) and drives it through the core `loadCardPacks` → `mergeMainStreetCardPool` (via `loadMainStreetCardPacks`), applies the pool, sets up a game, serializes, resets to base, and deserializes — asserting the same pool (templates, active packs, checksum) is restored.
- Missing-pack degradation is asserted: a pack recorded in a save but not installed produces a base-content pool plus a "missing" warning, and live card instances refuse to resume only when their template is genuinely unavailable.
- `npm test -- --project unit` and `npm run build` pass in this repo.

## Test Plan
- New `tests/main-street/CardPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts`; run `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/CardPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts`, then the full unit profile and build.
data.title: End-to-end card-pack pipeline integration test (loader → merge → save/load)
